column3: Generous; natural and at ease: 大 "big" plus 方 "manner". Free with money (对朋友很大方) and also relaxed in manner (举止大方). It can also mean tasteful (款式大方). The second syllable is neutral in speech: dàfang. The opposite of 小气 "stingy".
column6: Tā duì péngyou hěn dàfang.
column7: She is very generous to her friends.

column3: Warm-hearted, eager to help: 热 "warm" plus 心 "heart". Said of someone who readily helps others or takes part: 热心人, 热心帮助. It describes willingness to help, unlike 热情, which is more about warmth in welcome. 热 has 灬 "fire" at the bottom.
column6: Línjūmen dōu hěn rèxīn.
column7: The neighbors are all very helpful.

column3: Naive, innocent: 天 "heaven, natural" plus 真 "true". Describes a child's pure manner (天真的笑容), or an adult who is too trusting (你太天真了). Good for a child, mildly critical for an adult. The idea is "natural and true, not yet shaped by the world".
column6: Háizi de xiàoróng hěn tiānzhēn.
column7: The child's smile is so innocent.

column3: Naughty, mischievous: 调 "tease" plus 皮 "skin". A child who plays tricks or does not listen: 调皮的孩子, 调皮捣蛋. A mild word, even affectionate. 调 is tiáo here, as in 调皮, not diào in 调查. 皮 shows a hand stripping a hide.
column6: Zhège háizi hěn tiáopí.
column7: This child is very naughty.

column3: Careless, thoughtless: 粗 "coarse" plus 心 "heart, mind". A slip made without attention: 粗心大意, 太粗心了, 因为粗心做错题. About not looking closely; its opposite is 细心. 粗 has 米 "grain" and 且, a grain that is not finely milled.
column6: Tā zuò tí zǒngshì hěn cūxīn.
column7: He is always careless when doing the exercises.

column3: Stupid, clumsy, slow: 我太笨了, 笨手笨脚 "clumsy". A blunt word; with a friend it may be teasing, said of a stranger it is rude. It may be about brains or about hands. 笨 has ⺮ "bamboo" over 本; both parts are simple.
column6: Wǒ tài bèn le, yòu zuòcuò le.
column7: I am so stupid; I got it wrong again.

column3: Capable, able: 能 "can" plus 干 "do". A praise for a person who gets things done: 能干的人, 精明能干. Often said of a woman or a worker. Here 干 is gàn "do"; the traditional 幹 shows it, while 乾 and 干 as "dry" are gān.
column6: Tā shì ge nénggàn de rén.
column7: She is a capable person.

column3: Calm, level-headed: 冷 "cool" plus 静 "still". A person who stays composed in a crisis: 保持冷静 "keep calm", 冷静思考 "think calmly". It describes the mind, not the weather. Of a place, "quiet, deserted" is less common.
column6: Yùdào wèntí yào lěngjìng.
column7: When you meet a problem, stay calm.

column3: Self-confident, self-confidence: 自 "self" plus 信 "trust". Both as a noun (有自信) and an adjective (他很自信). Positive; for too much of it use 自大 or 骄傲. 自 is a picture of a nose, which people point to when they mean themselves.
column6: Tā duì zìjǐ hěn zìxìn.
column7: He is very confident in himself.

column3: Noble, lofty: 高 "high" plus 尚 "esteem". Used of morals, character, aims and acts: 高尚的品德, 高尚的人. Always positive and a little formal. Not about social class or taste; for refined taste use 高雅.
column6: Tā yǒu yī kē gāoshàng de xīn.
column7: He has a noble heart.

column3: To concentrate: 专 "single" plus 心 "mind". Verb-object, as adverb or verb: 专心学习, 专心听讲, 不专心. Its opposite is 分心. The idea is giving the whole mind to one thing.
column6: Shàngkè yào zhuānxīn tīngjiǎng.
column7: In class you must listen attentively.

column3: Simple, pure, naive: 单 "single" plus 纯 "pure". A person's mind or a plain thing: 想法单纯, 单纯的孩子. Also an adverb, "merely": 单纯为了钱 "just for money". 纯 has 纟 "silk" and 屯, pure silk.
column6: Tā de xiǎngfǎ hěn dānchún.
column7: Her way of thinking is very simple.

column3: To do one's best: 尽 "exhaust" plus 力 "strength". Verb-object: 尽力而为 "do all one can", 我会尽力. After it comes the thing to do: 尽力帮你. In the traditional 盡, a bowl 皿 is empty. 尽 is read jìn here.
column6: Wǒ huì jìnlì bāng nǐ.
column7: I will do my best to help you.

column3: Silent, taciturn: 沉 "sink" plus 默 "silent". To say nothing, from calm or for lack of words: 保持沉默, 沉默寡言. A person who speaks little, or a silence in a conversation. 沉 has 氵 and 冗; 默 has 黑 "black" and 犬 "dog".
column6: Tā chénmò le hěn jiǔ.
column7: He stayed silent for a long time.

column3: Silently, quietly: the doubled 默 "silent". An adverb before the verb: 默默地工作, 默默地付出 "give quietly, without seeking credit". Often with 地. It praises someone's quiet, unnoticed effort.
column4: 她默默地帮助了很多人。
column5: 她默默地幫助了很多人。
column6: Tā mòmò de bāngzhù le hěn duō rén.
column7: She quietly helped many people.

column3: Dear, beloved: 亲 "close" plus 爱 "love". Always before a noun, as in 亲爱的朋友, 亲爱的妈妈, the usual opening of a letter. Used in the way English uses "dear". In speech 亲爱的 is also an endearment between couples. The apostrophe separates qīn'ài.
column6: Qīn'ài de péngyou, nǐ hǎo!
column7: Dear friend, hello!

column3: Close, intimate: 亲 "close" plus 密 "dense". About a relationship or contact: 亲密的朋友, 关系亲密, 亲密接触. It describes the closeness of two people. 密 has 宀 and 山.
column6: Tāmen shì qīnmì de péngyou.
column7: They are close friends.

column3: To cherish, to take care of: 爱 "love" plus 护 "protect". Objects are things that need care: 爱护公物, 爱护环境, and also children or animals. In signs and rules: 请爱护花草. 护 has 扌 "hand" and 户, the sound.
column6: Qǐng àihù gōnggòng cáiwù.
column7: Please take care of public property.

column3: Patriotic, to love one's country: 爱 "love" plus 国 "country". Verb-object, but mostly used as an adjective: 爱国精神, 爱国者. In the simplified 国, a jade 玉 sits in a border 囗. Formal and common in official talk.
column6: Tā shì yī ge àiguó de rén.
column7: He is a patriotic person.

column3: To be fond of, to like: 喜 "like" plus 爱 "love". The object is a person, an animal or a thing: 喜爱音乐, 深受喜爱. More formal and warmer than 喜欢, and often passive: 受到喜爱 "be loved by". The apostrophe separates xǐ'ài.
column4: 孩子们都喜爱这只小狗。
column5: 孩子們都喜愛這隻小狗。
column6: Háizimen dōu xǐ'ài zhè zhī xiǎogǒu.
column7: The children all love this puppy.

column3: To break up, to part: 分 "divide" plus 手 "hand". Said of lovers who end a relationship: 他们分手了, 和女朋友分手. Also, more literally, of people who part ways after being together. Verb-object, so 分了手. 分 combines 八 "divide" with 刀 "knife".
column6: Tāmen qùnián fēnshǒu le.
column7: They broke up last year.

column3: Date, appointment; to meet by arrangement: 约 "arrange" plus 会 "meet". As a noun for a date between two people (一个约会) or an appointment. As a verb: 他们约会了. In mainland usage, rather romantic; for a business appointment use 预约.
column6: Tāmen zhōumò yǒu yī ge yuēhuì.
column7: They have a date at the weekend.

column3: To get along with each other: 相 "mutually" plus 处 "dwell". People living or working together: 和同事相处, 相处得很好/不好. Read xiāngchǔ, with 处 as a verb chǔ, not the noun chù. The 得 comes after, to show how it goes.
column6: Wǒ hé tóngshì xiāngchǔ de hěn hǎo.
column7: I get along very well with my colleagues.

column3: To gather, to get together: 聚一聚 "get together for a while", 聚在一起 "gather together". For friends and family meeting: 好久不见，聚一聚. The object is people, rarely things. 聚 shows several people 乑 with a hand taking an ear 取 and gives the sense of "together".
column4: 好久不见，我们聚一聚吧。
column5: 好久不見，我們聚一聚吧。
column6: Hǎojiǔ bù jiàn, wǒmen jù yī jù ba.
column7: Long time no see; let's get together.

column3: Party, get-together: 聚 "gather" plus 会 "meeting". Friends, classmates or a family: 开聚会, 同学聚会 "class reunion", 参加聚会. Both a noun and a verb "to get together". Less formal than 宴会 "banquet".
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen yǒu yī ge jùhuì.
column7: We have a get-together at the weekend.

column3: Social contact, to socialize: 交 "associate" plus 际 "between". About being sociable: 交际能力, 社交 is a close word. 很会交际 "good with people". 交际花 is a socialite. 交 shows a person with crossed legs.
column6: Tā hěn huì jiāojì.
column7: He is good at socializing.

column3: To visit someone out of concern: 看 "look" plus 望 "gaze". The object is a sick person, an elder or a friend: 看望病人, 看望老人. It implies a caring visit and the visitor is often younger or well. Not for a place or a business visit.
column6: Wǒ qù yīyuàn kànwàng péngyou.
column7: I am going to the hospital to visit a friend.

column3: To come to someone's home: 上 "go up to" plus 门 "door". Used for a service that comes to your house: 上门服务, 医生上门. Also "to call on": 上门拜访. In another sense it is "to close a shop". Context shows which; the first is the common one.
column6: Yīshēng shàngmén gěi tā kànbìng.
column7: The doctor came to his home to treat him.

column3: Thin, for flat things: 薄纸, 薄衣服, 薄被子. It is read báo in speech and bó in written compounds such as 薄弱 "weak". Figuratively, "slight, meagre": 薄利 "small profit". Opposite 厚. Its 艹 top suggests plant material, and 溥 gives the sound.
column6: Zhè běn shū hěn báo.
column7: This book is very thin.

column3: Thick: 厚书, 厚被子, 厚衣服 "heavy clothing", 厚度 "thickness". Also "generous, kind" in 厚道 and 深厚 "deep (of feelings)". Opposite 薄. Used of flat things; a thick rope is 粗, not 厚. The 厂 on the left is a cliff.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài hòu le.
column7: This garment is too thick.

column3: Thick, for long round things: 粗绳子, 粗手指, 粗腿. Also "coarse, rough": 粗心, 粗糙, and a "gruff voice". Opposite 细. For a flat thing that is thick, use 厚. 粗 has 米 "grain" and 且: coarse grain.
column6: Zhè gēn shéngzi hěn cū.
column7: This rope is very thick.

column3: Thin, slender, fine: 细绳子, 细雨 "drizzle", 细沙 "fine sand". Also "careful, detailed": 仔细, 细心. Opposite 粗. Use it for thin round things; a thin flat thing is 薄. 细 has 纟 "thread" and 田.
column6: Tā de shǒuzhǐ yòu xì yòu cháng.
column7: Her fingers are slender and long.

column3: Wide, broad: 宽路, 宽肩膀. Also loose (宽松) and generous or lenient (宽大). Opposite 窄. A measurement: 三米宽. 宽 has 宀 "roof", a wide room.
column6: Zhè tiáo lù hěn kuān.
column7: This road is very wide.

column3: Vast, broad: 宽 "wide" plus 广 "extensive". For land, sea, sky and also a broad mind: 宽广的草原, 心胸宽广. Larger and more literary than 宽. 广 is a lean-to roof 厂 with a dot, and the traditional 廣 has a part inside.
column6: Cǎoyuán fēicháng kuānguǎng.
column7: The grassland is extremely vast.

column3: Shallow: 浅水, 河很浅. Also pale in color (浅色) and simple (浅显), and "not deep" in a person's experience: 经验浅. Opposite 深. 浅 has 氵 "water" and 戋; it recalls a shallow water body.
column6: Zhè tiáo hé hěn qiǎn.
column7: This river is very shallow.

column3: Deep, profound for feelings and foundations: 深 "deep" plus 厚 "thick". 深厚的友谊, 深厚的感情, 深厚的基础. It is used for abstract things, never for water or holes. Both characters are measures of a layer; together they show weight.
column4: 他们之间有深厚的友谊。
column5: 他們之間有深厚的友誼。
column6: Tāmen zhījiān yǒu shēnhòu de yǒuyì.
column7: There is a deep friendship between them.

column3: Round, circle: 圆形, 圆桌, 月亮圆了 "the moon is full". Also 圆 as a unit of money (the written form of 元), and "to round off" in 圆满. The 囗 around the outside is a circle; 员 gives the sound.
column6: Jīnwǎn de yuèliang yòu dà yòu yuán.
column7: The moon tonight is big and round.

column3: Huge, enormous: 巨 "huge" plus 大 "big". Used for size and degree, and often before nouns such as 变化, 影响, 压力, 成功: 巨大的变化. Said of abstract things as often as of objects. A strong word, more formal than 很大.
column4: 这个城市发生了巨大的变化。
column5: 這個城市發生了巨大的變化。
column6: Zhège chéngshì fāshēng le jùdà de biànhuà.
column7: Huge changes have taken place in this city.

column3: Large-scale, large: 大 "big" plus 型 "type". It appears before a noun: 大型活动, 大型商场, 大型演出. Used for events, machines, companies. Opposite 小型. It is a modifier only; you do not say 这个很大型.
column6: Zhè shì yī chǎng dàxíng yǎnchū.
column7: This is a large-scale show.

column3: Small-scale, compact: 小 "small" plus 型 "type". Before a noun: 小型公司, 小型汽车, 小型音乐会. Opposite 大型. Unlike 小, it classes something as a size category; a small thing is just 小.
column6: Tā kāi le yī jiā xiǎoxíng gōngsī.
column7: He opened a small company.

column3: New type, new-style: 新 "new" plus 型 "type". Before a noun, for products and ideas: 新型手机, 新型材料, 新型冠状病毒. It says the thing is of a recently developed kind. Opposite 老式.
column6: Zhè shì yī zhǒng xīnxíng shǒujī.
column7: This is a new type of phone.

column3: Type, model, mold, mainly in compounds: 血型 "blood type", 发型 "hairstyle", 脸型 "face shape", 类型 "type". Its 土 "earth" recalls a clay mold; 刑 gives the sound. It is seldom used alone.
column6: Nǐ shì shénme xuèxíng?
column7: What is your blood type?

column3: To sink: 沉到水底, 沉下去. Also "heavy" (这个箱子很沉) and "deep" (沉睡 "sleep deeply"), and "to lower" (沉住气 "keep calm"). The sense depends on the context. 氵 "water" with 冗 shows something sinking.
column6: Shítou chén dào le shuǐdǐ.
column7: The stone sank to the bottom of the water.

column3: Heavy, often of mood or burden: 沉 "sink" plus 重 "heavy". 心情沉重, 沉重的负担 "a heavy burden", 脚步沉重. Not for a box you lift: that is just 重 or 沉. A literary, serious word. 重 here is zhòng.
column6: Tā de xīnqíng hěn chénzhòng.
column7: He feels heavy at heart.

column3: Ruler or a Chinese foot (about a third of a meter): 一尺长, 用尺量. The word is mostly in compounds: 尺子, 尺寸, 卷尺 "tape measure". In traditional systems 尺 is divided into 寸. The character shows a body 尸 with a pacing step.
column6: Tā yòng chǐ huà le yī tiáo xiàn.
column7: He drew a line with a ruler.

column3: Ruler: 尺 "ruler" plus the suffix 子. The everyday word for the plastic or wooden ruler used at school: 一把尺子, 借尺子. The suffix 子 is neutral (chǐzi). A tape measure is 卷尺.
column6: Qǐng bǎ chǐzi jiè gěi wǒ.
column7: Please lend me your ruler.

column3: Size, measurements: 尺 plus 寸, two old units. 尺寸 is used for the size of clothes, shoes and furniture: 尺寸合适 "fits right", 量尺寸 "take measurements". Also figuratively "propriety", in spoken use: 有分寸 is the more usual phrase. The second syllable is neutral.
column6: Zhè shuāng xié de chǐcun bù héshì.
column7: The size of these shoes does not fit.

column3: Centimeter: 厘 is a hundredth, 米 is a meter. After a number: 一百八十厘米. Taiwan usually says 公分. Read límǐ. 厘 has 厂 "cliff" and 里 inside; in Taiwan the traditional form is 釐 in this word.
column4: 他的身高一百八十厘米。
column5: 他的身高一百八十釐米。
column6: Tā de shēngāo yībǎi bāshí límǐ.
column7: He is 180 centimeters tall.

column3: Millimeter: 毫 is a thousandth, 米 is a meter. After a number: 五毫米. 毫 has 毛 "hair" beneath a top part: the finest hair. Taiwan also says 公釐. In general speech centimeters are used for everyday size.
column4: 这块板的厚度是五毫米。
column5: 這塊板的厚度是五毫米。
column6: Zhè kuài bǎn de hòudù shì wǔ háomǐ.
column7: This board is five millimeters thick.

column3: Milliliter: 毫 "thousandth" plus 升 "liter". After a number: 五百毫升. The drink bottle sizes you see on packages: 500毫升. 升 is the liter; Taiwan also says 公升.
column6: Zhè píng shuǐ yǒu wǔbǎi háoshēng.
column7: This bottle of water holds five hundred milliliters.

column3: Square, the second power: 三的平方是九. In area: 平方米 "square meter", 平方公里 "square kilometer". The unit is nearly always 平方米. Opposite 立方 "cube". 平 gives the "level" and 方 the "square".
column6: Sān de píngfāng shì jiǔ.
column7: The square of three is nine.

column3: Average; evenly: 平 "level" plus 均 "even". As verb or adverb: 平均每天, 平均分数. And as "evenly": 平均分配. In a sentence the average comes before the verb: 平均每天睡七个小时. 均 has 土 and 匀.
column4: 他每天平均睡七个小时。
column5: 他每天平均睡七個小時。
column6: Tā měitiān píngjūn shuì qī ge xiǎoshí.
column7: On average he sleeps seven hours a day.

column3: Times, -fold: 两倍 "twice as much", 三倍. After a number, as a measure word: 他的年纪是我的两倍. Note 增加了两倍 vs. 是…的两倍; the second is the safer pattern. 倍 is also "double" as a verb in 加倍.
column6: Tā de niánjì shì wǒ de liǎng bèi.
column7: He is twice my age.

column3: Here liáng, "to measure": 量身高, 量体温, 量一量. It is a verb, and the noun "quantity" is liàng, as in 数量. The same character, two reads. The verb often doubles: 量一量. The 旦 over 里 gives the picture of measuring a field.
column6: Qǐng yòng chǐ liáng yi liáng.
column7: Please measure it with a ruler.

column3: Weight: 重 "heavy" plus 量 "amount". The number a scale gives: 重量是十公斤. Compare 体重, which is the weight of a person. 重 is zhòng here, "heavy". 量 is liàng, the "quantity" reading.
column4: 这个箱子的重量是十公斤。
column5: 這個箱子的重量是十公斤。
column6: Zhège xiāngzi de zhòngliàng shì shí gōngjīn.
column7: This box weighs ten kilograms.

column3: To measure, to test: 测体温 "take a temperature", 测一下, 预测 "predict". On its own it is a verb with a tool or a quantity as object. 测 has 氵 "water", from measuring water depth, and 则 for sound.
column6: Qǐng nǐ cè yīxià tǐwēn.
column7: Please take your temperature.

column3: To measure, to survey: 测 "measure" plus 量 "measure". Used for land, height, distance, and for instruments: 测量身高, 测量工具. Here 量 is liáng. Suitable for careful measuring; 量 alone is the everyday word.
column6: Gōngrén zhèngzài cèliáng zhè kuài dì.
column7: The workers are surveying this plot of land.

column3: To test; a test: 测 "measure" plus 试 "try". A trial of a person's skill (汉语水平测试) or of a machine or program (测试软件). Also a noun. Less official than 考试, which is a school exam. 试 has 讠 and 式.
column6: Míngtiān yǒu Hànyǔ cèshì.
column7: There is a Chinese test tomorrow.

column3: Model, type number: 型 "type" plus 号 "number". The exact model of a product: 手机型号, 什么型号. Used when buying, repairing or ordering. 型 on its own means type; 号 turns it into the specific code.
column6: Zhège shǒujī shì shénme xínghào?
column7: What model is this phone?

column3: Extremely: 极了 comes after an adjective: 好极了, 美极了, 累极了. Alone as an adverb before an adjective: 极好, 极大. As a noun, "pole": 北极, 南极. 极了 is a spoken pattern that works with feelings and states.
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng měi jíle.
column7: The scenery here is extremely beautiful.

column3: Extremely: 极 "extreme" plus 其 "that". A formal intensifier that goes before an adjective or verb: 极其重要, 极其困难. Stronger than 很 or 非常, and more written. It does not go after the word, unlike 极了.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì jíqí zhòngyào.
column7: This matter is extremely important.

column3: Especially, particularly: 格 "standard" plus 外 "beyond". It goes before an adjective and means more than usual for the occasion: 格外高兴, 格外冷. It compares the situation with the ordinary one, so it often follows a time phrase.
column6: Jīntiān de tiānqì géwài hǎo.
column7: The weather today is especially good.

column3: Excessive, going too far: 过 "exceed" plus 分 "limit". An adjective for words or acts: 太过分了, 过分的要求 "an excessive demand". Often a criticism: 你太过分了 "you went too far". 分 is fèn here, "limit".
column6: Tā shuō de yǒudiǎn guòfèn.
column7: What he said was a bit much.

column3: Ample, sufficient; fully: 充 "fill" plus 分 "portion". Before a noun: 充分的准备, 充分的理由. As an adverb: 充分利用 "make full use of". More formal and positive than 很多. 充分 is a good fit with abstract nouns such as 准备 and 理由.
column6: Nǐ yào zuòhǎo chōngfèn de zhǔnbèi.
column7: You must make ample preparation.

column3: Thorough, completely: 彻 "penetrate" plus 底 "bottom". An adjective and adverb: 彻底解决 "solve once and for all", 彻底改变 "change completely". Down to the bottom. It suits cleaning, changes and failures. 底 is dǐ here.
column6: Fángjiān yào chèdǐ dǎsǎo yīxià.
column7: The room needs a thorough cleaning.

column3: Used in 非…不可 "must, nothing else will do": 他非要去不可 "he insists on going". Also "not", in 非常 "very", 非法 "illegal", and "wrong" in 是非. The sense "insist" is the one to learn here. 非 is two wings pointing opposite ways.
column6: Tā fēi yào qù bùkě.
column7: He insists on going.

column3: Almost, nearly: 几 "few" plus 乎 "particle". It goes before a verb or number, and says something is close to the case: 几乎每天, 几乎没有 "almost none". With a negative it can mean "hardly": 几乎不. Read jīhū, with 几 as jī, not jǐ.
column6: Wǒ jīhū měitiān dōu pǎobù.
column7: I run almost every day.

column3: Easily, lightly: 轻 "light" plus 易 "easy". It is nearly always negative: 不会轻易放弃 "won't give up easily", 不要轻易相信. The meaning is "casually, without thought". You rarely see it in a positive sentence. 轻 has 车 and a sound part.
column6: Tā bù huì qīngyì fàngqì.
column7: He will not give up easily.

column3: Even, so much so that: 甚 "extreme" plus 至 "reach". It names an extreme example at the end of a list or a rise: 他忙得甚至忘了吃饭. Often with 都 or 也 afterward. Written and spoken. The form 甚至于 is rare.
column6: Tā máng de shènzhì wàng le chīfàn.
column7: He was so busy that he even forgot to eat.

column3: On the contrary, instead: 反 "opposite" plus 而 "but". It points to a result opposite to what one would expect: 雨没有停，反而更大了. Do not use it merely for contrast between two things; the expectation is turned upside down. The apostrophe marks fǎn'ér.
column6: Yǔ méiyǒu tíng, fǎn'ér gèng dà le.
column7: The rain did not stop; it got even heavier.

column3: Mostly, for the most part: 大 "big" plus 多 "many". Before a verb or a noun phrase: 大多是…, 大多数人. It states what the majority is: 这里的学生大多是外国人. For "most people", the fuller 大多数 with 人. 多 in the old script shows two pieces of meat.
column4: 这里的学生大多是外国人。
column5: 這裡的學生大多是外國人。
column6: Zhèlǐ de xuésheng dàduō shì wàiguórén.
column7: The students here are mostly foreigners.

column3: In total, altogether: 总 "sum" plus 共 "together". Before a number: 总共十个, 总共多少钱. It adds up everything. The word 一共 is the same in meaning and more common in speech. 共 shows two hands holding something.
column6: Wǒmen zǒnggòng yǒu shí ge rén.
column7: There are ten of us in all.

column3: Individual, a few: 个 "single" plus 别 "separate". As an attribute: 个别学生 "a few of the students", 个别情况 "isolated cases". It points to a small number out of many, the exceptions. Also "individually": 个别谈话 "talk one-on-one".
column4: 个别学生没有完成作业。
column5: 個別學生沒有完成作業。
column6: Gèbié xuésheng méiyǒu wánchéng zuòyè.
column7: A few students did not finish the homework.

column3: Each, every, all the various: 各 "each" plus 个 "item". Before a noun, with no 的: 各个方面 "every aspect", 各个班. It treats a group as separate members. Also "one by one": 各个击破. 各 shows a foot 夂 and a mouth 口.
column6: Gègè bān dōu cānjiā le bǐsài.
column7: Every class took part in the contest.

column3: The rest, the remainder: 其 "that" plus 余 "remaining". Before a noun with 的, or alone: 其余的人 "the others". 其余 is all that remain after you have named some.
column6: Qíyú de rén dōu huí jiā le.
column7: The rest of the people all went home.

column3: All alike, without exception: 一 "one" plus 律 "rule". An adverb before the verb: 一律平等 "all equal", 一律免费 "free for all". Used for rules and notices. Here 律 is lǜ, written "lv" in pinyin input.
column6: Xuésheng yīlǜ chuān xiàofú.
column7: All students wear the school uniform without exception.

column3: Single, odd, bill, list: 单数 "odd number", 菜单 "menu", 账单 "bill", 名单 "list". As a verb-object in 买单 "pay the bill". Alone it mostly appears in compounds. Also read Shàn as a surname.
column6: Fúwùyuán, mǎidān!
column7: Waiter, the bill please!

column3: Alone, separately: 单 "single" plus 独 "alone". Before a verb: 单独行动, 单独谈话 "talk in private". It stresses being apart from others, by choice or need. 独 has 犭 "dog" and 虫; a lone animal.
column6: Tā xǐhuan dāndú lǚxíng.
column7: He likes to travel alone.

column3: Alone, by oneself: 独 "alone" plus 自 "self". An adverb before a verb: 独自生活, 独自一人. A written word, with a tone of loneliness or independence. Not about being in a room with no one, but about acting without a companion.
column6: Tā dúzì yī rén qù le Běijīng.
column7: She went to Beijing all by herself.

column3: Individual: 个 "single" plus 体 "body". A single member, as opposed to the group: 个体差异 "individual differences". Also in 个体户 "self-employed trader", the original use in China. Mostly written or technical.
column6: Měi ge gètǐ dōu bùtóng.
column7: Every individual is different.

column3: Countless: 无 "without" plus 数 "number". Before a measure word or noun: 无数颗星星, 无数次 "countless times". A figure of speech, not a count. The reading of 数 here is shù ("number"); as a verb "to count" it is shǔ.
column6: Tiān shàng yǒu wúshù kē xīngxing.
column7: There are countless stars in the sky.

column3: Unlimited, infinite: 无 "no" plus 限 "limit". Before a noun or as predicate: 无限的可能, 无限大, 无限期. Common in set phrases of feeling too: 无限感激. The opposite is 有限. 限 has 阝 "mound" and 艮; a boundary.
column4: 孩子的想象力是无限的。
column5: 孩子的想像力是無限的。
column6: Háizi de xiǎngxiànglì shì wúxiàn de.
column7: A child's imagination is boundless.

column3: Limited: 有 "have" plus 限 "limit". 时间有限, 能力有限, 有限公司 "limited company". It says there is a limit, often a small one. Sometimes politely: 我的能力有限 "my ability is limited". The opposite is 无限.
column6: Wǒ de shíjiān yǒuxiàn.
column7: My time is limited.

column3: Diverse, varied: 多 "many" plus 样 "kind". Describes variety: 丰富多样, 多样化 "diversify", 多样性 "diversity". Mostly used with 丰富 or in nouns with 性. It is not used to mean "many kinds of" before a noun; for that use 多种.
column6: Chéngshì de shēnghuó fēngfù duōyàng.
column7: City life is rich and varied.

column3: Many kinds of, various: 多 "many" plus 种 "kind". Before a noun: 多种颜色, 多种方式. A stable quantity word. 种 is zhǒng "kind" here, with 禾 "grain"; as "to plant" it is zhòng. It comes before the noun, without 的 for most uses.
column4: 这里有多种颜色可以选择。
column5: 這裡有多種顏色可以選擇。
column6: Zhèlǐ yǒu duōzhǒng yánsè kěyǐ xuǎnzé.
column7: There are various colors to choose from.

column3: One of: after the group, with 的: 最大的城市之一 "one of the biggest cities". The 之 links, as 的 would, and 一 is the number. A common pattern: 之一 ends a noun phrase and cannot be moved. In writing and in speech alike.
column4: 北京是中国最大的城市之一。
column5: 北京是中國最大的城市之一。
column6: Běijīng shì Zhōngguó zuì dà de chéngshì zhīyī.
column7: Beijing is one of China's largest cities.

column3: Used in fractions: 三分之一 "one third" (three parts, of which one), 百分之五十 "fifty percent". The denominator comes first, the numerator after 之. Say the bottom number first. 分 is fēn here, "part", and 之 acts like "of".
column6: Sān fēnzhī yī de xuésheng méi lái.
column7: One third of the students did not come.

column3: Accountant; accounting: 会 "reckon" plus 计 "count". A person (她是会计) or the field (学会计). Note the reading kuàijì, not huìjì. 会 reads kuài only in this word and a few related ones.
column6: Tā shì gōngsī de kuàijì.
column7: She is the company's accountant.

column3: Lawyer: 律 "law" plus 师 "master". The ending 师 names a skilled professional: 老师, 医师, 工程师. 当律师, 请律师 "hire a lawyer". 律 is lǜ. 师 has 巾 and a knife-like part in the simplified form.
column6: Tā shì yī míng lǜshī.
column7: He is a lawyer.

column3: Secretary: 秘 "secret" plus 书 "writing". Someone who handles letters and schedules for a boss: 秘书长 "secretary-general". 秘 is mì here, as in 秘密. The traditional form is 祕書 in Taiwan; 秘 has 禾 where 祕 has 礻.
column4: 秘书把文件放在桌子上。
column5: 秘書把文件放在桌子上。
column6: Mìshū bǎ wénjiàn fàng zài zhuōzi shàng.
column7: The secretary put the document on the table.

column3: To work overtime: 加 "add" plus 班 "shift". Verb-object: 加了班, 加班到很晚. 经常加班 "often work late". A big part of working life in China. 加 is 力 "strength" plus 口 "mouth": add something on.
column6: Wǒ jīnwǎn yào jiābān.
column7: I have to work overtime tonight.

column3: To handle matters, to run errands: 办 "handle" plus 事 "affair". Verb-object: 办了事, 办事处 "office". Often an official errand: 去银行办事. In a different sense, "to work": 办事认真 "works conscientiously".
column6: Tā zài yínháng bànshì.
column7: He is at the bank taking care of some business.

column3: To hold a post, to serve as: 担 "bear" plus 任 "duty". The post comes after: 担任班长, 担任经理 "work as manager". For an official role or position; 做 is the plain word. 担 is dān here, "take on".
column6: Tā dānrèn bānzhǎng.
column7: He serves as the class monitor.

column3: Pay and conditions, treatment: 待 "treat" plus 遇 "meet". Used for salary and benefits (待遇很好) and also for how someone is treated (受到不同的待遇). In job ads, "待遇面议" means pay is negotiated. 遇 has 辶 "walk".
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de dàiyù hěn hǎo.
column7: This company has good pay and benefits.

column3: Unemployed; to lose one's job: 失 "lose" plus 业 "work". Verb-object: 失了业, 失业率 "unemployment rate". The cause of being out of work, not just a lack of job; for someone who has a long break, 待业 is used.
column6: Tā qùnián shīyè le.
column7: He lost his job last year.

column3: Spare-time, amateur: 业 "work" plus 余 "remaining". Outside working hours: 业余爱好 "hobby", 业余时间. Also "amateur" as opposed to a professional: 业余选手. The opposite is 专业.
column6: Tā de yèyú àihào shì huàhuà.
column7: His hobby is painting.

column3: Trade, industry, line of work: 行 "line" plus 业 "business". Used for a whole field: 教育行业, 服务行业, 哪个行业. The first syllable is háng, not xíng. 行 shows two steps, a crossroad, and háng is "row".
column6: Tā zài jiàoyù hángyè gōngzuò.
column7: He works in the education industry.

column3: Identity, status: 身 "person" plus 份 "portion". Who one is: 身份证 "ID card", 他的身份是老师 "he is a teacher". Also capacity: 以老师的身份 "as a teacher". Taiwan writes 身分 more often. Read shēnfèn.
column6: Tā de shēnfèn shì lǎoshī.
column7: He is a teacher by profession.

column3: Position, status: 地 "place" plus 位 "rank". Social, political or economic standing: 社会地位, 地位高. Also the importance of something: 重要的地位. 位 combines 亻 and 立, a person standing in place.
column6: Nǚxìng de dìwèi yuè lái yuè gāo.
column7: Women's status is getting higher and higher.

column3: Sales clerk: 售 "sell" plus 货 "goods" plus 员 "person". Someone who sells things in a shop. 售 shows a bird 隹 and 口. 员 ends titles of people: 服务员, 运动员. In everyday speech, 营业员 and 店员 are close.
column6: Shòuhuòyuán zài zhěnglǐ huòjià.
column7: The sales clerk is arranging the shelves.

column3: Model (fashion): a loanword from English "model", with 儿 ending: mótèr. 当模特儿 "work as a model". The 儿 ending is northern; Taiwan says 模特兒 and the last syllable is neutral. Without the 儿, 模特 is the same word.
column6: Tā xiǎng dāng mótèr.
column7: She wants to be a model.

column3: Business card: 名 "name" plus 片 "card". 递名片 "hand over a card", 交换名片. In business, it is given and received with two hands. 名 shows a mouth 口 under the evening moon 夕: calling one's name in the dark.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ de míngpiàn.
column7: This is my business card.

column3: Résumé, CV: 简 "brief" plus 历 "experience". 写简历, 投简历 "send out a résumé", 发简历. 简 has ⺮ "bamboo" and 间; bamboo slips for brief writing. 历 is the simple form of 歷 "experience".
column6: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de jiǎnlì fā gěi wǒ.
column7: Please send me your résumé.

column3: Interview for a job or school: 面 "face" plus 试 "test". Verb and noun: 参加面试, 面试通过, 我去面试. 面 here is a face in the sense of face to face. Compare 采访, an interview by a reporter.
column6: Míngtiān wǒ yǒu yī ge miànshì.
column7: I have an interview tomorrow.

column3: To apply for: 申 "state" plus 请 "request". The object is a place, loan, visa or job: 申请签证, 申请大学, 申请表 "application form". Done in writing. 申 started as a picture of lightning.
column6: Wǒ shēnqǐng le yī suǒ dàxué.
column7: I applied to a university.

column3: Training; to train: 培 "cultivate" plus 训 "instruct". Short-term professional courses: 参加培训, 新员工培训. 培 uses 土 "earth", as in tending plants. A person undergoing training is a 受训者.
column6: Gōngsī gěi xīn yuángōng péixùn.
column7: The company trains its new staff.

column3: Training class, cram school: 培训 "training" plus 班 "class". Extra courses after work or school: 报培训班 "sign up for a course", 英语培训班. The 班 shows a jade cut in two, "to divide" into classes.
column4: 我报了一个英语培训班。
column5: 我報了一個英語培訓班。
column6: Wǒ bào le yī ge Yīngyǔ péixùnbān.
column7: I signed up for an English training class.

column3: To cultivate, to foster: 培 "cultivate" plus 养 "raise". Objects: talents, habits, interests, feelings: 培养兴趣, 培养人才, 培养习惯. A longer, patient process than 培训. Also for raising plants and cells.
column4: 父母要培养孩子的兴趣。
column5: 父母要培養孩子的興趣。
column6: Fùmǔ yào péiyǎng háizi de xìngqù.
column7: Parents should cultivate their children's interests.

column3: To nurture, to breed: 培 "cultivate" plus 育 "bring up". Used for plants and animals (培育新品种 "breed a new variety") and in writing for people (培育人才). More formal than 培养. 育 shows a baby in a womb.
column4: 这所学校培育了很多人才。
column5: 這所學校培育了很多人才。
column6: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào péiyù le hěn duō réncái.
column7: This school has nurtured many talents.

column3: Opportunity, chance: 机 "occasion" plus 遇 "meet". A fortunate turn of events: 抓住机遇, 难得的机遇. Often paired with 挑战: 机遇与挑战. Compare 机会, which is the everyday "chance"; 机遇 is bigger and rarer.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge nándé de jīyù.
column7: This is a rare opportunity.

column3: Future prospects: 前 "ahead" plus 途 "road". About career and life ahead: 前途光明 "a bright future", 没有前途. Applies to a person, a job or a company. 途 has 辶 "walk" and 余 as the sound.
column6: Tā de qiántú yī piàn guāngmíng.
column7: His future is bright.

column3: Skill, technique: 技 "skill" plus 巧 "clever". The method of doing something well: 写作技巧, 技巧高超. The technique is learned and practiced. 技 has 扌 "hand" and 支 as the sound. 巧 is also "skillful".
column6: Xiězuò xūyào yīxiē jìqiǎo.
column7: Writing needs some technique.

column3: Skilled, proficient: 熟 "familiar" plus 练 "practice". Of a person who does something well after practice: 熟练工人, 熟练掌握. Describes both the skill and the speed. 熟 here is shú; in speech it is also shóu. 练 has 纟 "thread".
column6: Tā dǎzì hěn shúliàn.
column7: She types very skillfully.

column3: To be good at: 善 "good" plus 于 "at". Followed by a verb: 善于沟通, 善于学习. Describes a talent, a trait. More formal than 会 or 擅长 (nearly the same). Cannot be used with a noun object directly.
column6: Tā shànyú hé rén jiāoliú.
column7: She is good at communicating with people.

column3: Intelligence, mental ability: 智 "wisdom" plus 力 "power". In 智力测验 "intelligence test", 开发智力 "develop the mind". An abstract and slightly technical word; for a person who is clever use 聪明. 智 has 知 "know" over 日.
column4: 这个游戏可以锻炼智力。
column5: 這個遊戲可以鍛鍊智力。
column6: Zhège yóuxì kěyǐ duànliàn zhìlì.
column7: This game can train the mind.

column3: Enterprise, company: 企 "undertake" plus 业 "business". Suits businesses of any size, especially in official talk: 国有企业, 私营企业, 企业家 "entrepreneur". More formal than 公司. 企 shows a person 人 on tiptoe 止.
column4: 这家企业有一千名员工。
column5: 這家企業有一千名員工。
column6: Zhè jiā qǐyè yǒu yīqiān míng yuángōng.
column7: This company has a thousand employees.

column3: Organization, institution: 机 "mechanism" plus 构 "structure". A body with a job: 研究机构, 金融机构, 政府机构. It is wider than 公司, and can mean a bank, a school or an office. Also the inner structure of a body.
column4: 他在一个国际机构工作。
column5: 他在一個國際機構工作。
column6: Tā zài yī ge guójì jīgòu gōngzuò.
column7: He works at an international organization.

column3: Engineering project, construction work: 工 "work" plus 程 "course". A big job with a plan: 建筑工程, 重大工程, 工程师 "engineer". It stands for the work itself and for the project. 工 shows a worker's tool.
column4: 这个工程要三年才能完成。
column5: 這個工程要三年才能完成。
column6: Zhège gōngchéng yào sān nián cái néng wánchéng.
column7: This project will take three years to complete.

column3: Project; item, event: 项 "item" plus 目 "heading". A planned piece of work (新项目, 项目经理) or an event in a sports meet (比赛项目). The word fits business and science alike. 目 is a picture of an eye turned sideways.
column4: 我们正在做一个新项目。
column5: 我們正在做一個新項目。
column6: Wǒmen zhèngzài zuò yī ge xīn xiàngmù.
column7: We are working on a new project.

column3: Contract: 合 "join" plus 同 "same". A legal agreement: 签合同, 劳动合同 "work contract", 合同到期. Written and binding. Taiwan says 合約 or 契約. The second syllable is neutral in speech: hétong.
column6: Qǐng zài hétóng shàng qiānzì.
column7: Please sign the contract.

column3: Scale, size: 规 "rule, pattern" plus 模 "model". How big an enterprise or event is: 规模大/小, 扩大规模, 具有一定规模. Said of companies, events and projects, not objects. 模 is mó here.
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de guīmó hěn dà.
column7: This company is very large.

column3: Large-scale: 大 "big" plus 规模 "scale". Before a verb or noun: 大规模生产, 大规模建设. Used for plans, campaigns and production. Opposite 小规模. Like 规模 it does not describe a single object.
column6: Zhèngfǔ kāishǐ dàguīmó jiànshè.
column7: The government began large-scale construction.

column3: Efficiency: 效 "effect" plus 率 "rate". 工作效率 "work efficiency", 效率高/低, 提高效率. A measure of speed against result. 率 is lǜ ("rate") here; as a verb "to lead" it is shuài. 效 has 攵 "strike" and 交.
column6: Tā gōngzuò xiàolǜ hěn gāo.
column7: He works very efficiently.

column3: Here huà, "to draw (a line), to mark off": 划线 "draw a line", 划重点 "mark the key points". With other readings, huá is "to row" (划船). Also "to plan" in 计划 and 规划, where it is read huà too. 划 uses 刂 "knife" for cutting a line.
column4: 请在这个词下面划一条线。
column5: 請在這個詞下面劃一條線。
column6: Qǐng zài zhège cí xiàmiàn huà yī tiáo xiàn.
column7: Please draw a line under this word.

column3: Plan, scheme, proposal: 方 "method" plus 案 "plan". A worked-out plan for acting: 设计方案, 解决方案 "solution", 三个方案. More detailed than 计划. The apostrophe marks the syllable break in fāng'àn.
column6: Wǒmen tǎolùn le sān ge fāng'àn.
column7: We discussed three plans.

column3: To carry out, to put into effect: 实 "real" plus 施 "apply". Laws, plans and policies: 实施计划, 开始实施, 全面实施. Written and official. The thing is the object, or the subject with 开始实施. Compare 执行, to carry out an order.
column4: 新规定下个月开始实施。
column5: 新規定下個月開始實施。
column6: Xīn guīdìng xià ge yuè kāishǐ shíshī.
column7: The new rules take effect next month.

column3: To do business, to be open: 营 "operate" plus 业 "business". Shops and restaurants: 营业时间 "opening hours", 开始营业, 停止营业. Notice the sign 营业中 "open".
column4: 商店早上九点开始营业。
column5: 商店早上九點開始營業。
column6: Shāngdiàn zǎoshang jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ yíngyè.
column7: The shop opens at nine in the morning.

column3: Business, commercial affairs: 商 "trade" plus 务 "affairs". It modifies a noun: 商务舱 "business class", 商务旅行, 商务会议. Not the same as 生意, which is a deal or trade. More formal; a word of offices and travel.
column6: Tā chángcháng yīn shāngwù qù Běijīng.
column7: He often goes to Beijing on business.

column3: Agent, intermediary: 中 "between" plus 介 "go between". A person or firm who connects two sides, most often in housing: 房产中介, 找中介. Also a verb, "to mediate". 介 is a person 人 between two marks.
column4: 我通过中介找到了房子。
column5: 我通過中介找到了房子。
column6: Wǒ tōngguò zhōngjiè zhǎodào le fángzi.
column7: I found the house through an agent.

column3: To keep something going in its present state: 维持秩序 "keep order", 维持生活 "make a living", 维持现状 "keep things as they are". 维 on its own means "hold together" and 持 "hold", so the two characters say the same thing twice. It needs an object and is neutral to formal in tone.
column6: Tā kào dǎgōng wéichí shēnghuó.
column7: He makes a living by doing odd jobs.

column3: To safeguard, uphold, maintain: the object is usually something abstract or valued, such as 权利 "rights", 和平 "peace" or 安全 "safety": 维护自己的权利. Unlike 维修, it is not about mending a machine. The 护 means "protect".
column6: Wǒmen yào wéihù shìjiè hépíng.
column7: We must safeguard world peace.

column3: Maintenance and repair of equipment, buildings and vehicles, as a noun (维修费 "repair costs", 维修站 "repair shop") or a verb. 维 "keep up" plus 修 "repair". It is the word on signs and notices: 电梯正在维修 "the elevator is under repair".
column4: 电梯正在维修，请走楼梯。
column5: 電梯正在維修，請走樓梯。
column6: Diàntī zhèngzài wéixiū, qǐng zǒu lóutī.
column7: The elevator is being repaired, please use the stairs.

column3: To repair, fix a concrete thing: 修理自行车 "fix a bicycle", 修理电脑. A repair person is 修理工. In speech it also means "to sort someone out, teach them a lesson": 我要修理你！ The object always follows the verb directly.
column4: 我的手机坏了，要拿去修理。
column5: 我的手機壞了，要拿去修理。
column6: Wǒ de shǒujī huài le, yào ná qù xiūlǐ.
column7: My phone is broken and has to be taken to be repaired.

column3: As a noun, "device, apparatus, installation": 安全装置 "safety device", 控制装置 "control unit". It is more technical than 机器 and names a built-in part of a larger system. As a verb, "to install", it is less common than 安装.
column4: 这台机器有一个安全装置。
column5: 這台機器有一個安全裝置。
column6: Zhè tái jīqì yǒu yī ge ānquán zhuāngzhì.
column7: This machine has a safety device.

column3: Facilities, installations: the buildings and equipment that serve a purpose, as in 公共设施 "public facilities", 体育设施 "sports facilities", 医疗设施. It is a collective noun and is not counted with 个; say 这些设施 or 设施齐全 "fully equipped".
column4: 这个小区的设施很齐全。
column5: 這個小區的設施很齊全。
column6: Zhège xiǎoqū de shèshī hěn qíquán.
column7: This residential area is very well equipped.

column3: On its own, it mostly means "peaceful, safe" in compounds (平安, 安全, 安静), and "to install, fit": 安灯 "put in a lamp", 安空调 "install an air conditioner". The picture is a woman 女 under a roof 宀, a sign of safety. As a verb it takes a concrete object and a place with 在.
column6: Qǐng nǐ bǎ dēng ān zài zhèlǐ.
column7: Please put the lamp in here.

column3: To find a place for, settle a person or thing: 安置难民 "settle refugees", 安置行李 "stow the luggage". It suggests that someone arranges things properly, often after a move or a crisis. The object is usually a person or group that needs housing or work.
column4: 政府为受灾的人安置了住处。
column5: 政府為受災的人安置了住處。
column6: Zhèngfǔ wèi shòuzāi de rén ānzhì le zhùchù.
column7: The government found places to live for the people hit by the disaster.

column3: Both a verb ("to fix in place": 把桌子固定住) and an adjective ("fixed, regular"): 固定工作 "a steady job", 固定时间 "a set time", 固定的收入 "a regular income". 固 means "firm, solid" and 定 "set". Opposite: 流动.
column4: 他每天在固定的时间跑步。
column5: 他每天在固定的時間跑步。
column6: Tā měitiān zài gùdìng de shíjiān pǎobù.
column7: He runs at a fixed time every day.

column3: The core idea is "to settle, fix": 定计划 "make a plan", 定时间 "set a time". It also means "to book or order": 定机票 "book a flight ticket", 订 is the usual character for that sense in writing. Also "settled, calm" in compounds like 安定. The roof 宀 over the character is a clue to "settling in a place".
column6: Wǒmen dìng le míngtiān de jīpiào.
column7: We have booked tomorrow's plane tickets.

column3: Steady, stable for things that do not wobble: 开得很稳 "drive steadily", 站稳 "stand firmly", and for people, "reliable": 他做事很稳. As a result complement, 稳 means "firmly": 坐稳了 "sit firmly", 拿稳 "hold steady". The 禾 grain on the left is a loose hint at "settled, secure".
column6: Qǐng zuò wěn le, chē yào kāi le.
column7: Please sit tight, the bus is about to go.

column3: Stable and "to stabilize": 情绪稳定 "emotionally stable", 物价稳定 "stable prices", 稳定下来 "settle down". It describes something that stays at an even level over time, and is used of the economy, a job, a relationship or feelings. 稳 is "steady" and 定 "fixed".
column6: Tā de gōngzuò hěn wěndìng.
column7: His job is very stable.

column3: Firm, solid, sturdy for physical things: 坚固的桥 "a sturdy bridge", 坚固的房子. It is about a structure that will not break or fall, not about being steady like 稳. Both characters mean "hard, firm". It can also be used figuratively: 坚固的友谊.
column6: Zhè zuò qiáo fēicháng jiāngù.
column7: This bridge is extremely sturdy.

column3: Smooth and steady: 飞机平稳地飞行 "the plane flies smoothly", 价格平稳 "prices are stable", 心情平稳. It stresses no ups and downs, no bumps. 平 is "level, flat" and 稳 "steady". The adverb form is 平稳地.
column6: Fēijī píngwěn de jiàngluò le.
column7: The plane landed smoothly.

column3: To guard, watch over: 守门 "guard a door" or "play goalkeeper", 守在门口 "stand watch at the door". It also means "to keep, abide by": 守规矩, 守时 "be punctual", 守信用 "keep one's word". In both senses you stay put and keep something safe. The 宀 roof over a hand 寸 shows someone keeping watch at home.
column6: Nǐ yào shǒu guījǔ, bùyào luàn pǎo.
column7: You must follow the rules and not run around.

column3: To close, shut, more formal than 关: 关闭窗户, 关闭电脑 "shut down the computer". Used for shops and institutions it means "to close down for good": 工厂被关闭了. Both characters mean "close". Everyday doors and lids take 关 alone.
column6: Shāngdiàn wǎnshang shí diǎn guānbì.
column7: The shop closes at ten in the evening.

column3: Without, not having, a written word that appears in set phrases: 无法 "unable", 无人 "nobody", 无关 "unrelated", 无意 "no intention". It is rarely used alone in speech, where 没有 takes its place. Also the prefix "un-/-less": 无用 "useless".
column4: 他无家可归，只好住在朋友家。
column5: 他無家可歸，只好住在朋友家。
column6: Tā wú jiā kě guī, zhǐhǎo zhù zài péngyou jiā.
column7: He had no home to go back to and had to stay at a friend's.

column3: Unable to, there is no way to: placed before a verb, 无法解释 "cannot explain", 无法相信. It is the written, slightly formal version of 没办法. It states that something is impossible, often for lack of means, and never takes 不 before it.
column6: Wǒ wúfǎ huídá zhège wèntí.
column7: I cannot answer this question.

column3: To look down on, despise: 看不起别人 "look down on others", 被人看不起. The structure is verb + 不 + result: "cannot look up (at)". The opposite is 看得起 "to think well of". Often used with 谁 and 别人: 谁也看不起他.
column4: 不要看不起任何一个人。
column5: 不要看不起任何一個人。
column6: Bùyào kànbuqǐ rènhé yī ge rén.
column7: Don't look down on anyone.

column3: Cannot stand, cannot bear: 热得受不了 "unbearably hot", 我受不了他 "I can't stand him". It is the 不 form of the potential complement 受得了. The 了 here is liǎo, which is a result marker meaning "be able to". Often used for complaints.
column6: Zhèlǐ tài chǎo le, wǒ shòubuliǎo.
column7: It's too noisy here, I can't stand it.

column3: Amazing, remarkable: praise for a person or an achievement: 你真了不起！ 他是个了不起的人. It can also be sarcastic: 有什么了不起的 "what's so great about that?". Structure: 了 (liǎo, "finish") + 不 + 起, "can't be finished", too much to be ordinary.
column4: 他十岁就会写诗，真了不起。
column5: 他十歲就會寫詩，真了不起。
column6: Tā shí suì jiù huì xiě shī, zhēn liǎobuqǐ.
column7: He could write poems at ten, which is amazing.

column3: Not enough time (to), too late (to): 来不及吃早饭 "no time to eat breakfast", 来不及了 "it's too late". The opposite is 来得及. It refers to a lack of time, not of ability. It follows the subject or a time word and is often followed by a verb.
column6: Kuài diǎnr, yào láibují le.
column7: Hurry up, we're running out of time.

column3: Cannot do without, inseparable from: 孩子离不开妈妈 "the child needs its mother", 离不开手机. Structure: 离 "leave" + 不 + 开 "away", "unable to leave". It names a strong dependence, and the opposite is 离得开.
column4: 现在的人都离不开手机。
column5: 現在的人都離不開手機。
column6: Xiànzài de rén dōu líbukāi shǒujī.
column7: Nowadays people can't do without their phones.

column3: Not to care, not mind: 他不在乎钱 "he doesn't care about money", 不在乎别人怎么说. It is the negative of 在乎 and is far more common than the positive. The thing you do not care about follows directly.
column4: 他一点儿也不在乎别人怎么说。
column5: 他一點兒也不在乎別人怎麼說。
column6: Tā yīdiǎnr yě bùzàihu biéren zěnme shuō.
column7: He doesn't care at all what other people say.

column3: To care about, mind: almost always in the negative or in questions: 你在乎吗？ 我在乎你的看法. A neutral tone on 乎 is normal. Compare 在乎 with 关心: 在乎 is about whether something matters to you, not about caring for someone's welfare.
column6: Nǐ zàihu tā de kànfǎ ma?
column7: Do you care what he thinks?

column3: It doesn't matter, I don't mind, said when you have no preference: 吃什么都无所谓 "I don't mind what we eat". 我无所谓 alone means "whatever, it's all the same to me". Said flatly it can sound uninterested. The form 无所谓 + noun "not a matter of ..." is more literary.
column4: 去哪儿吃饭我都无所谓。
column5: 去哪兒吃飯我都無所謂。
column6: Qù nǎr chīfàn wǒ dōu wúsuǒwèi.
column7: I don't mind where we go to eat.

column3: It doesn't matter, never mind, used to reassure someone: 没带伞不要紧 "it doesn't matter that you didn't bring an umbrella". Also "not serious": 他的病不要紧 "his illness is not serious". The 紧 is "tight, urgent", so 不要紧 is "not urgent". 没关系 is the more general reply to an apology.
column4: 没带伞不要紧，我有一把。
column5: 沒帶傘不要緊，我有一把。
column6: Méi dài sǎn bùyàojǐn, wǒ yǒu yī bǎ.
column7: It doesn't matter that you didn't bring an umbrella, I have one.

column3: Can't do anything about it, no way (to), the spoken, northern form of 没办法. 我没法儿去 "I have no way of going". The 儿 ending is part of the word and is pronounced as a quick r on 法. It is also a complete reply: 没法儿！ "Nothing to be done!". For writing, 没办法 or 无法 is safer.
column4: 雨太大了，我没法儿出门。
column5: 雨太大了，我沒法兒出門。
column6: Yǔ tài dà le, wǒ méifár chūmén.
column7: It's raining too hard, I can't go out.

column3: That's right, you're right, agreeing with someone: 你说得没错. Said alone, 没错！ means "exactly!" or "sure thing!". It can also reassure that something will not go wrong: 交给我，没错. Literally "there is no mistake". The 没 is méi here.
column4: 你说得没错，我今天太累了。
column5: 你說得沒錯，我今天太累了。
column6: Nǐ shuō de méicuò, wǒ jīntiān tài lèi le.
column7: You're right, I'm too tired today.

column3: Didn't expect, who would have thought: it introduces something surprising, often with 竟然 or 会: 没想到你也来了 "I didn't expect you to come too". A verb with 到 as result ("think of"), so the whole means "did not think of it (happening)". It can start a sentence or stand alone.
column6: Méixiǎngdào nǐ yě lái le!
column7: I didn't expect you to come too!

column3: There's still time (to), the positive partner of 来不及: 现在走还来得及 "it's still not too late if we leave now". Often used in questions: 来得及吗？ It follows the subject or a time word, and a verb may follow: 来得及赶上火车.
column6: Xiànzài chūfā hái láidejí.
column7: There's still time if we set off now.

column3: To convene, hold a meeting or conference, formal: 召开会议 "hold a meeting", 召开记者招待会 "hold a press conference". The subject is the organizer, and the thing convened is always a gathering. 召 means "call together", and 开 "open". Don't use it for a party or a class.
column4: 公司明天要召开一个会议。
column5: 公司明天要召開一個會議。
column6: Gōngsī míngtiān yào zhàokāi yī ge huìyì.
column7: The company will hold a meeting tomorrow.

column3: A general meeting, a congress, a big assembly: 全体大会 "plenary session", 运动大会 "sports meet", 股东大会 "shareholders' meeting". 大 "large" plus 会 "meeting". It is bigger and more formal than a plain 会议, and is held by a whole organization.
column4: 大会明天上午九点开始。
column5: 大會明天上午九點開始。
column6: Dàhuì míngtiān shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ.
column7: The general meeting starts at nine tomorrow morning.

column3: Chairperson, and also the title of the head of state or of an organization: 主席先生 "Mr. Chairman", 学生会主席 "head of the student union". 主 means "main" and 席 "seat". The 席 is a mat, the old way of sitting and so of having a place at a gathering. It is mostly a title, not a casual word.
column6: Tā shì xuéshēnghuì de zhǔxí.
column7: He is the chairman of the student union.

column3: A lecture, a talk given in a series or for the public: 听讲座 "go to a lecture", 举办讲座 "hold a talk". 讲 "talk" plus 座 "seat". The measure word is 个 or 场: 一场讲座. It is less formal than a university class, and open to anyone.
column4: 今天下午有一个关于健康的讲座。
column5: 今天下午有一個關於健康的講座。
column6: Jīntiān xiàwǔ yǒu yī ge guānyú jiànkāng de jiǎngzuò.
column7: There is a talk about health this afternoon.

column3: To give a speech and "a speech": 做演讲 or 发表演讲 "give a speech", 演讲比赛 "speech contest". 演 "perform" plus 讲 "speak" makes a speech aimed at an audience, usually prepared. As a verb it takes no object; the topic goes before: 在大会上演讲.
column4: 她在大会上做了一个精彩的演讲。
column5: 她在大會上做了一個精彩的演講。
column6: Tā zài dàhuì shang zuò le yī ge jīngcǎi de yǎnjiǎng.
column7: She gave a wonderful speech at the meeting.

column3: To report back to a superior or group about work or progress: 向经理汇报工作 "report on one's work to the manager". Also a noun, "report": 工作汇报. 汇 means "to gather together" and 报 "report", so the report brings the facts together. It goes upward, from junior to senior, unlike 通知.
column6: Wǒ yào xiàng jīnglǐ huìbào gōngzuò.
column7: I have to report on my work to the manager.

column3: To seek, ask for opinions or suggestions: 征求意见 "ask for comments", 征求大家的看法. The object is almost always 意见, 建议 or 看法, and the person asked comes before with 向 or 对. It is somewhat formal. Both 征 and 求 carry the idea of "seeking".
column6: Lǎoshī zhēngqiú dàjiā de yìjiàn.
column7: The teacher asks everyone for their opinions.

column3: To pass on a message to a third person: 请转告他 "please tell him (for me)", 转告老师. You received something and relay it. The 转 here means "to turn, pass along", and 告 "tell". It is polite and fixed for messages, with a person as indirect object.
column6: Qǐng nǐ zhuǎngào tā, míngtiān kāihuì.
column7: Please tell him that there is a meeting tomorrow.

column3: To remind: 提醒我 "remind me", 提醒你带伞 "remind you to bring an umbrella". It can also mean "to warn": 提醒大家注意安全. The person reminded is the object, followed by what to do. 提 "raise" plus 醒 "wake up": to wake someone up to something. Not the same as 记得 "remember".
column6: Qǐng tíxǐng wǒ míngtiān dài sǎn.
column7: Please remind me to bring an umbrella tomorrow.

column3: To persuade, convince someone: 说服他 "convince him", 被说服 "be persuaded". 说 "speak" plus 服 "submit": talk someone round. You can persuade a person to do something: 说服他去看医生. 服 is the same character as in 服从 "obey" and 佩服 "admire".
column6: Wǒ shuōfú le tā qù kàn yīshēng.
column7: I persuaded him to go and see a doctor.

column3: To admit, acknowledge: 承认错误 "admit a mistake", 不敢承认. Also "to recognize" a country, a result, a fact: 承认事实. 承 "take on" plus 认 "recognize". It means accepting something that is true, often unwelcome, so it suits mistakes and facts.
column6: Tā chéngrèn shì zìjǐ de cuò.
column7: He admitted it was his own fault.

column3: To confirm, verify: 确认时间 "confirm the time", 确认订单 "confirm an order", 请确认 "please confirm". 确 "certain" plus 认 "recognize". You use it for checking details and for pressing "confirm" on a website. Unlike 承认, it is neutral and has nothing to do with guilt.
column6: Qǐng zài quèrèn yīxià shíjiān.
column7: Please confirm the time once more.

column3: To talk about, discuss in an informal or gossipy way, often behind someone's back: 议论别人 "gossip about others", 大家都在议论这件事. As a noun it is "talk, comments": 引起议论. It is less orderly than 讨论, which is a proper exchange of views.
column6: Dàjiā dōu zài yìlùn zhè jiàn shì.
column7: Everyone is talking about this.

column3: To argue, dispute, a heated exchange of opposing views: 争论不休 "argue without end", 引起争论 "cause a controversy", also a noun, "debate". 争 "fight over" plus 论 "discuss". The topic comes first or after 关于/对: 他们为这件事争论了很久.
column4: 他们为这件事争论了很久。
column5: 他們為這件事爭論了很久。
column6: Tāmen wèi zhè jiàn shì zhēnglùn le hěn jiǔ.
column7: They argued about this for a long time.

column3: To debate: a more formal contest of arguments, as in 辩论赛 "a debate competition" and 辩论队 "debate team". 辩 means "argue a case" and 论 "discuss". Unlike 争论, which can be an angry quarrel, 辩论 has structure, with two sides defending a position.
column4: 学校举办了一场辩论赛。
column5: 學校舉辦了一場辯論賽。
column6: Xuéxiào jǔbàn le yī chǎng biànlùnsài.
column7: The school held a debate competition.

column3: To interview or "to cover a story", as a reporter does: 采访市长 "interview the mayor", 接受采访 "give an interview". 采 "gather" plus 访 "visit". It is journalism: a reporter gathers news by visiting people. For a job interview use 面试.
column4: 记者正在采访那位运动员。
column5: 記者正在採訪那位運動員。
column6: Jìzhě zhèngzài cǎifǎng nà wèi yùndòngyuán.
column7: The reporter is interviewing that athlete.

column3: To take part in, be involved in: 参与活动 "take part in an activity", 参与讨论 "join a discussion", 参与者 "participant". The reading of 与 is yù here, not yǔ. It is a bit more formal than 参加 and emphasizes involvement in a process, often planning or decision-making.
column4: 每个人都可以参与这个活动。
column5: 每個人都可以參與這個活動。
column6: Měi ge rén dōu kěyǐ cānyù zhège huódòng.
column7: Everyone can take part in this activity.

column3: To join an organization or group, or "to add in": 加入俱乐部 "join a club", 加入我们 "join us", 往汤里加入一点盐 "add some salt to the soup". 加 "add" plus 入 "enter". With people, it means becoming a member, unlike 参加, which is for attending an event.
column4: 我想加入你们的足球队。
column5: 我想加入你們的足球隊。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng jiārù nǐmen de zúqiúduì.
column7: I'd like to join your football team.

column3: To attend a formal event, meeting or ceremony: 出席会议 "attend a meeting", 出席婚礼. 出 "go out" plus 席 "seat": you take your seat. It suits formal gatherings and important guests, and the opposite is 缺席 "be absent". It is not used for a class or a casual party.
column4: 总统将出席明天的会议。
column5: 總統將出席明天的會議。
column6: Zǒngtǒng jiāng chūxí míngtiān de huìyì.
column7: The president will attend tomorrow's meeting.

column3: To gather, assemble at a set time and place: 在门口集合 "meet at the gate", 八点集合. It is what a leader says to a group: 大家集合！ The people come together from various places. In math it is "a set", which is why the word appears in school texts.
column4: 明天早上七点在学校门口集合。
column5: 明天早上七點在學校門口集合。
column6: Míngtiān zǎoshang qī diǎn zài xuéxiào ménkǒu jíhé.
column7: We'll meet at the school gate at seven tomorrow morning.

column3: To imagine and "imagination": 想象不到 "can't imagine", 难以想象 "hard to imagine", 丰富的想象力 "a rich imagination". 想 "think" plus 象 "image, picture": you form a picture in your mind. The common frame is 我想象不到 or 你想象一下.
column4: 你想象一下，一百年以后会怎么样。
column5: 你想象一下，一百年以後會怎麼樣。
column6: Nǐ xiǎngxiàng yīxià, yībǎi nián yǐhòu huì zěnmeyàng.
column7: Imagine what things will be like in a hundred years.

column3: To think deeply about, reflect on: 思考问题 "think a problem over", 独立思考 "think for yourself". 思 is "think" and 考 "examine". It is more serious and slower than 想, and suits problems, life, choices. Usually without a plain object like a person.
column4: 遇到问题时，先要认真思考。
column5: 遇到問題時，先要認真思考。
column6: Yùdào wèntí shí, xiān yào rènzhēn sīkǎo.
column7: When you meet a problem, you first need to think seriously.

column3: To consider, think over a decision or plan: 考虑一下 "think it over", 考虑清楚 "think it through", 值得考虑. It is also a noun: 这是我的考虑. 考 "examine" plus 虑 "ponder". Used when weighing options before deciding, so it fits offers, plans and choices.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ yào kǎolǜ yīxià.
column7: I need to think this over.

column3: Doubt, question, the noun for a doubt about something: 有疑问 "have questions", 毫无疑问 "without a doubt", 提出疑问. 疑 "doubt" plus 问 "ask". In an exam or class, 有什么疑问吗？ is a polite way to ask "any questions?". 毫无疑问 is a very common set phrase.
column4: 如果你有疑问，可以问老师。
column5: 如果你有疑問，可以問老師。
column6: Rúguǒ nǐ yǒu yíwèn, kěyǐ wèn lǎoshī.
column7: If you have questions, you can ask the teacher.

column3: To understand, know about; to find out: 了解情况 "learn the situation", 我不太了解他 "I don't know him well". It is about gaining knowledge of someone or something's real nature, not about grasping a language point, for which you use 懂. 了 is liǎo here, not le.
column4: 我想了解一下这个城市。
column5: 我想了解一下這個城市。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng liǎojiě yīxià zhège chéngshì.
column7: I'd like to find out more about this city.

column3: To summarize a text or an argument in a few words: 概括起来说 "to sum up", 概括一下 "summarize it". Also "to generalize". 概 means "general, approximate" and 括 "to bundle". It can be used as an adjective-like adverb as well: 概括地说 "in brief". Unlike 总结, it condenses what is already there.
column4: 请你用一句话概括这篇文章。
column5: 請你用一句話概括這篇文章。
column6: Qǐng nǐ yòng yī jù huà gàikuò zhè piān wénzhāng.
column7: Please sum up this article in one sentence.

column3: One-sided, biased: a view that sees only one part of the matter: 看问题很片面 "look at things in a one-sided way", 片面的看法. 片 "piece" plus 面 "side". It is a criticism of a judgment or opinion, not of a person's character. Often with 太, 很 or 过于.
column6: Nǐ de kànfǎ tài piànmiàn le.
column7: Your view is too one-sided.

column3: To overlook, neglect, ignore something that matters: 忽视问题 "ignore a problem", 不能忽视. 忽 means "suddenly, careless" and 视 "look at". The object is usually an important point or a risk, and the word is a mild criticism. It is more formal than 不管.
column4: 我们不能忽视孩子的感受。
column5: 我們不能忽視孩子的感受。
column6: Wǒmen bù néng hūshì háizi de gǎnshòu.
column7: We cannot overlook the children's feelings.

column3: To choose and "a choice": 选择专业 "choose a major", 做出选择 "make a choice", 没有选择 "no choice". 选 and 择 both mean "pick". It suits a considered decision between several options, more serious than 挑. In a quiz it means "multiple choice": 选择题.
column4: 我选择留在这个城市工作。
column5: 我選擇留在這個城市工作。
column6: Wǒ xuǎnzé liú zài zhège chéngshì gōngzuò.
column7: I chose to stay and work in this city.

column3: Details, particulars: 注意细节 "pay attention to the details", 工作中的细节, 细节决定成败. 细 "fine, thin" plus 节 "section, point". Usually plural in English but with no measure word: 很多细节. Used for the small points of a plan, story or task.
column4: 我们还要讨论一下计划的细节。
column5: 我們還要討論一下計劃的細節。
column6: Wǒmen hái yào tǎolùn yīxià jìhuà de xìjié.
column7: We still need to talk through the details of the plan.

column3: Careful, meticulous, fine: 工作细致 "careful in work", 细致的观察 "close observation". It says something is done with great attention to detail, as a compliment for a person's work or for a piece of craft. 细 "fine" plus 致 "delicate". Often with 很 or 非常.
column6: Tā zuòshì fēicháng xìzhì.
column7: She does things very carefully.

column3: Conclusion, what you decide after looking at things: 得出结论 "come to a conclusion", 下结论 "draw a conclusion", 还没有结论 "no conclusion yet". 结 "tie up" plus 论 "discuss". It appears at the end of a study, argument or meeting, so it suits both research and everyday reasoning. 下结论太早 means "too early to judge".
column6: Xiànzài xià jiélùn hái tài zǎo.
column7: It's still too early to draw a conclusion.

column3: Common sense, general knowledge: 生活常识 "everyday know-how", 缺乏常识, 没有常识. 常 "ordinary" plus 识 "knowledge". It means basic things everyone is expected to know, such as health or safety rules, more than IQ. The measure word is 点: 一点常识. The 识 is read shí here.
column4: 这是一个生活常识，大家都应该知道。
column5: 這是一個生活常識，大家都應該知道。
column6: Zhè shì yī ge shēnghuó chángshí, dàjiā dōu yīnggāi zhīdào.
column7: This is basic everyday knowledge that everyone should know.

column3: Psychology, mental state: 心理健康 "mental health", 心理学 "the science of psychology", 儿童心理, 心理压力 "psychological pressure". 心 "heart/mind" plus 理 "reason, pattern". It describes the inner state of a person or group, not the body. Compare 心情 "mood", which is a passing feeling.
column4: 孩子的心理健康很重要。
column5: 孩子的心理健康很重要。
column6: Háizi de xīnlǐ jiànkāng hěn zhòngyào.
column7: Children's mental health is very important.

column3: Dream, ambition as a noun, and "to dream of" as a verb: 实现梦想 "realize a dream", 梦想成为医生. 梦 "dream" plus 想 "think". It is a hope you want to achieve, not a sleeping dream, which is 梦. It is strong and positive, and often appears with 追求 and 实现.
column4: 他的梦想是成为一名医生。
column5: 他的夢想是成為一名醫生。
column6: Tā de mèngxiǎng shì chéngwéi yī míng yīshēng.
column7: His dream is to become a doctor.

column3: To inspect, make a study visit: 实地考察 "an on-the-spot study", 考察市场, 出国考察. 考 "examine" plus 察 "observe". People go to a place to see for themselves, as officials, scholars or business people do. It differs from 参观, which is for sightseeing. Used mainly in a work context.
column4: 他们去山区考察当地的教育情况。
column5: 他們去山區考察當地的教育情況。
column6: Tāmen qù shānqū kǎochá dāngdì de jiàoyù qíngkuàng.
column7: They went to the mountain area to study its local education.

column3: To hint, suggest and "a hint": 暗示他 "give him a hint", 心理暗示 "self-suggestion", 一个暗示. 暗 "dark, hidden" plus 示 "show", so you show it indirectly, without saying it outright. It is used when someone says one thing and means another, in speech, gestures or looks.
column6: Tā ànshì wǒ zǎodiǎn huí jiā.
column7: She hinted that I should go home early.

column3: Perhaps, maybe, a written-style adverb that comes before the verb or at the start: 或许他已经走了 "perhaps he has already left". 或 "or" plus 许 "allow". It is less strong than 一定 and about as formal as 也许, which is a little more common in speech. It cannot stand alone as an answer.
column6: Huòxǔ tā jīntiān bù huì lái le.
column7: Perhaps he won't come today.

column3: Maybe, can't say for sure, a spoken word: 说不定会下雨 "it may rain", 他说不定已经到了. It is literally "can't say it is fixed". It comes before the verb or as a short opinion, and implies a real chance. Often followed by 会 or a verb phrase.
column4: 带上伞吧，说不定会下雨。
column5: 帶上傘吧，說不定會下雨。
column6: Dài shàng sǎn ba, shuōbudìng huì xià yǔ.
column7: Take an umbrella, it might rain.

column3: Not necessarily: 未必是真的 "may not be true", 贵的未必好 "expensive isn't necessarily good". 未 is the written "not yet" and 必 is "must", so "not certain". It is a gentle doubt that does not deny outright. It goes before the verb or adjective and often follows a statement you are partly rejecting.
column6: Guì de dōngxi wèibì hǎo.
column7: Expensive things are not necessarily good.

column3: Hard to avoid, inevitable: 难免会犯错 "will inevitably make mistakes", 这是难免的. 难 "difficult" plus 免 "avoid". The speaker says something is bound to happen for a reason, often with 会 before the verb. It may also be the complement: 错误是难免的.
column4: 学习一门新语言时，难免会犯错。
column5: 學習一門新語言時，難免會犯錯。
column6: Xuéxí yī mén xīn yǔyán shí, nánmiǎn huì fàncuò.
column7: When learning a new language, you will inevitably make mistakes.

column3: It seems, apparently, a written adverb placed before a verb or adjective: 他似乎不高兴 "he seems unhappy", 似乎有点儿冷. The speaker has an impression, not proof. It sounds more formal than 好像, which is the usual word in speech. Often goes with 有点.
column6: Tā jīntiān sìhū bù tài gāoxìng.
column7: He doesn't seem very happy today.

column3: As if, like, put after a noun or phrase: 像雪似的那么白 "white as snow", 他高兴得像孩子似的. Often with 像 or 好像: 好像没睡似的. The 似 here is read shì, not sì. 的 is neutral. It marks a comparison or an impression.
column4: 他高兴得像个孩子似的。
column5: 他高興得像個孩子似的。
column6: Tā gāoxìng de xiàng ge háizi shìde.
column7: He is as happy as a child.

column3: Whether (or not), formal: 不知道是否 "don't know whether", 是否同意 "whether one agrees". 是 "be" plus 否 "not". It replaces 是不是 or 有没有 in writing and sits inside a clause, not at the end. It is not used on its own as a question in speech.
column6: Wǒ bù zhīdào tā shìfǒu tóngyì.
column7: I don't know whether he agrees.

column3: It seems, it looks as if, used at the start to give a conclusion from what you can see: 看来要下雨了 "it looks like rain", 看来你很忙. 看 "look" plus 来 as a direction. The 来 is neutral. It differs from 似乎, as it builds on the evidence in front of you.
column6: Kànlái míngtiān yào xià yǔ le.
column7: It looks like it will rain tomorrow.

column3: It can be seen (that), so clearly: it begins a conclusion drawn from what was said before: 他每天练习，可见很努力 "he practices every day, so he is clearly hard-working". Also "visible": 清晰可见. As a connector, it comes at the start of the second clause.
column4: 他每天练习两小时，可见他很努力。
column5: 他每天練習兩小時，可見他很努力。
column6: Tā měitiān liànxí liǎng xiǎoshí, kějiàn tā hěn nǔlì.
column7: He practices two hours every day, so he is clearly hard-working.

column3: Generally speaking, an opener before a statement that holds in most cases: 一般来说，冬天比较冷. It is a set phrase, with a comma after it. You can add exceptions afterwards with 但是. 一般 is "ordinary, in general" and 来说 "speaking of".
column4: 一般来说，北方的冬天比较冷。
column5: 一般來說，北方的冬天比較冷。
column6: Yībānláishuō, běifāng de dōngtiān bǐjiào lěng.
column7: Generally speaking, winters in the north are rather cold.

column3: In short, in a word: it introduces a summing-up after several points: 总之，你要小心 "in short, be careful". It comes at the start of a sentence with a comma. 总 means "total" and 之 is a written "it". It is written or formal, and stresses that details do not change the outcome.
column4: 不管怎样，总之你要小心。
column5: 不管怎樣，總之你要小心。
column6: Bùguǎn zěnyàng, zǒngzhī nǐ yào xiǎoxīn.
column7: Whatever happens, in short, you must be careful.

column3: Really, indeed, to confirm or concede something: 他的确很聪明 "he really is clever", 的确如此 "that is indeed so". 的确 reads dí-què: 的 is read dí here, not de. It comes before the verb or adjective. Often agrees with a previous statement.
column4: 这家餐厅的菜的确很好吃。
column5: 這家餐廳的菜的確很好吃。
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài díquè hěn hǎochī.
column7: The food in this restaurant is indeed very tasty.

column3: On earth, actually, for pressing a question: 你究竟想怎么样？ "what on earth do you want?", 究竟是谁？ It goes after the subject before the verb. As a noun it means "the outcome": 弄个究竟 "get to the bottom of it". It adds impatience, so 到底 can replace it.
column6: Nǐ jiūjìng xiǎng qù nǎr?
column7: Where on earth do you want to go?

column3: Unexpectedly, to my surprise: 他竟然忘了我的生日 "he actually forgot my birthday". It goes before the verb and shows that something went against expectations, good or bad. 竟 means "unexpectedly" and 然 "so". It is stronger than 居然, which is nearly the same.
column4: 他竟然忘了自己的生日。
column5: 他竟然忘了自己的生日。
column6: Tā jìngrán wàng le zìjǐ de shēngrì.
column7: He actually forgot his own birthday.

column3: Research, study as a noun, "to research, look into" as a verb: 研究问题 "study a problem", 做研究 "do research", 研究生 "graduate student". 研 and 究 both mean "investigate" (研 is "grind", 究 "get to the bottom"). In speech it also means "to discuss and decide": 我们研究一下.
column6: Tā zài dàxué lǐ yánjiū lìshǐ.
column7: He studies history at the university.

column3: To develop, research and make a product, medicine or machine: 研制新药 "develop a new drug", 研制成功 "be successfully developed". 研 "research" plus 制 "make". It involves both research and making, so it applies to things that did not exist before. It does not mean the study of a topic.
column4: 科学家们研制出了一种新药。
column5: 科學家們研製出了一種新藥。
column6: Kēxuéjiāmen yánzhì chū le yī zhǒng xīn yào.
column7: The scientists developed a new medicine.

column3: Statistics; to count up: 统计数字 "statistical figures", 统计人数 "count the people", 据统计 "according to statistics". 统 "all together" plus 计 "count". As a verb it adds up a whole; as a noun it is the field or the numbers. 据统计 is a common way to start a report.
column4: 据统计，这个城市有一千万人口。
column5: 據統計，這個城市有一千萬人口。
column6: Jù tǒngjì, zhège chéngshì yǒu yī qiān wàn rénkǒu.
column7: According to statistics, this city has ten million people.

column3: Materials, data, information, things used for study or reference: 查资料 "look up materials", 学习资料 "study materials", 个人资料 "personal data". 资 "resources" plus 料 "material". It is an uncountable noun that covers documents and facts, not the news. A single item is 一份资料.
column6: Wǒ zhèngzài wǎng shang chá zīliào.
column7: I'm looking up material online.

column3: To predict, forecast and "a forecast": 预测天气 "forecast the weather", 无法预测 "unpredictable", 预测结果. 预 "in advance" plus 测 "measure". It is based on data, so it differs from 猜 "guess". It is less formal than 预报, which names weather forecasts.
column6: Méiyǒu rén néng yùcè wèilái.
column7: No one can predict the future.

column3: Trend, tendency: 发展趋势 "development trend", 上升的趋势 "a rising trend", 有……的趋势. 趋 "move toward" plus 势 "momentum". It names the direction in which something is going over time, as in economics or society. It takes 的 before: 增长的趋势.
column6: Fángjià yǒu shàngshēng de qūshì.
column7: House prices tend to go up.

column3: Theme, subject of a talk, event, film or piece of writing: 今天的主题 "today's theme", 主题歌 "theme song", 主题公园 "theme park". 主 "main" plus 题 "topic". It names what the whole thing is about, and is a bit broader than 题目, which is the title or an exam question.
column4: 这次会议的主题是环境保护。
column5: 這次會議的主題是環境保護。
column6: Zhè cì huìyì de zhǔtí shì huánjìng bǎohù.
column7: The theme of this meeting is environmental protection.

column3: Background: the setting behind an event or a picture, or a person's origins. 历史背景 "historical background", 家庭背景 "family background", 背景音乐 "background music". 背 is "back" and 景 "scene", so the scene at the back. In slang, it also means a powerful backer: 他有背景.
column4: 这部电影的背景是二十年代的上海。
column5: 這部電影的背景是二十年代的上海。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng de bèijǐng shì èrshí niándài de Shànghǎi.
column7: The film is set in Shanghai in the 1920s.

column3: Comprehensive, composite; to synthesize: 综合考虑 "consider all together", 综合素质 "overall quality", 综合大学 "a university with many faculties". 综 "bring together" plus 合 "combine". It treats many parts as one whole and is often an adjective before a noun.
column4: 老师会综合大家的意见做决定。
column5: 老師會綜合大家的意見做決定。
column6: Lǎoshī huì zōnghé dàjiā de yìjiàn zuò juédìng.
column7: The teacher will make a decision by bringing everyone's views together.

column3: Things, matters, an abstract word for anything that exists, events and objects together: 新事物 "new things", 事物的发展 "the development of things", 各种事物. 事 "affair" plus 物 "object". It is written and rather philosophical, and has no measure word: 很多事物.
column4: 我们要用发展的眼光看事物。
column5: 我們要用發展的眼光看事物。
column6: Wǒmen yào yòng fāzhǎn de yǎnguāng kàn shìwù.
column7: We should look at things with an eye to development.

column3: Nature, character, quality of something, what kind it is: 工作性质 "the nature of the work", 问题的性质 "the nature of the problem". 性 "nature" plus 质 "substance". Used in analysis to classify things, usually followed by "of": 性质不同 "different in nature". The 质 is zhì, 4th tone.
column4: 这两个问题的性质不一样。
column5: 這兩個問題的性質不一樣。
column6: Zhè liǎng ge wèntí de xìngzhì bù yīyàng.
column7: The nature of these two problems is not the same.

column3: Characteristic, feature, trait: 基本特征 "basic characteristics", 个人特征, 面部特征 "facial features". 特 "special" plus 征 "sign". Both are concrete signs by which something can be recognized or told apart.
column4: 熊猫的特征是黑白两色。
column5: 熊貓的特徵是黑白兩色。
column6: Xióngmāo de tèzhēng shì hēibái liǎng sè.
column7: The characteristic of the panda is its black and white coloring.

column3: Situation, circumstances, especially a political or economic one that is changing: 国际形势 "the international situation", 经济形势, 形势很好. 形 "shape" plus 势 "power, tendency". It means the overall state and the way it is moving, and so is heard in news. It describes large-scale conditions, not a personal circumstance.
column6: Xiànzài de jīngjì xíngshì hěn hǎo.
column7: The economic situation is good now.

column3: To improve a situation or condition: 改善生活 "improve living conditions", 改善关系 "improve relations", 改善环境. 改 "change" plus 善 "good". The object is a condition, a state of affairs or relations, not a person's skills, for which use 提高. It often occurs with 得到: 得到改善.
column4: 医生的工作改善了病人的生活。
column5: 醫生的工作改善了病人的生活。
column6: Yīshēng de gōngzuò gǎishàn le bìngrén de shēnghuó.
column7: The doctor's work improved the patients' lives.

column3: To correct, put right a mistake or fault: 改正错误 "correct a mistake", 改正缺点 "fix a shortcoming". 改 "change" plus 正 "right". The object is a wrong thing in behavior or a text, and you do it yourself. 改错 is the casual form for fixing errors on homework.
column4: 发现错误后，他马上改正了。
column5: 發現錯誤後，他馬上改正了。
column6: Fāxiàn cuòwù hòu, tā mǎshàng gǎizhèng le.
column7: After finding the mistake, he corrected it at once.

column3: To shorten a time, distance or length: 缩短时间 "shorten the time", 缩短距离 "narrow the distance", 缩短工作时间. 缩 "contract" plus 短 "short". The opposite is 延长.
column4: 新的高铁缩短了两个城市的距离。
column5: 新的高鐵縮短了兩個城市的距離。
column6: Xīn de gāotiě suōduǎn le liǎng ge chéngshì de jùlí.
column7: The new high-speed railway has shortened the distance between the two cities.

column3: To reduce, shrink, narrow something in size or scope: 缩小范围 "narrow the scope", 缩小差距 "narrow the gap", 缩小图片 "make a picture smaller". 缩 "contract" plus 小 "small". It is the opposite of 扩大. The thing shrunk follows.
column6: Qǐng bǎ túpiàn suōxiǎo yīdiǎn.
column7: Please make the picture a little smaller.

column3: To expand, enlarge something's scope or size: 扩大范围 "widen the scope", 扩大影响 "increase influence", 扩大生产. 扩 "extend" plus 大 "big". The opposite is 缩小. It is used for abstract and concrete things alike, such as markets, a house or a group.
column6: Gōngsī dǎsuàn kuòdà shēngchǎn.
column7: The company plans to expand production.

column3: To extend, spread out: 扩展业务 "expand business", 向外扩展, 扩展到全国. 扩 "extend" plus 展 "unfold". Compared with 扩大, 展 gives the idea of stretching outward and reaching new areas. Also seen in computing: 扩展名 "file extension".
column4: 这家公司的业务扩展到了全国。
column5: 這家公司的業務擴展到了全國。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de yèwù kuòzhǎn dào le quánguó.
column7: This company's business has spread across the whole country.

column3: To lower, reduce something such as a price, level, cost or risk: 降低价格 "lower prices", 降低成本, 降低风险 "reduce risk". 降 "drop" plus 低 "low". The object follows, and it can also be intransitive, with a figure or level as the subject.
column4: 商店降低了水果的价格。
column5: 商店降低了水果的價格。
column6: Shāngdiàn jiàngdī le shuǐguǒ de jiàgé.
column7: The shop has lowered the price of fruit.

column3: To fall, decline, drop: the thing itself goes down, with no object: 气温下降 "the temperature drops", 成绩下降 "grades fall", 下降了百分之五. 下 "down" plus 降 "descend". The opposite is 上升. A planned lowering by someone uses 降低.
column6: Zuìjìn qìwēn míngxiǎn xiàjiàng le.
column7: The temperature has dropped noticeably recently.

column3: To fall, drop, descend, mostly in compounds: 降雨 "rainfall", 降温 "the temperature drops", 降价 "lower the price", 降落 "land". The 阝 on the left is a hill, and the idea is of going down a slope. In 投降 "surrender" the same character is read xiáng, which is worth knowing.
column4: 明天会降温，你要多穿点衣服。
column5: 明天會降溫，你要多穿點衣服。
column6: Míngtiān huì jiàngwēn, nǐ yào duō chuān diǎn yīfu.
column7: The temperature will drop tomorrow, so wear more clothes.

column3: To subtract, reduce: 减肥 "lose weight", 减价 "cut prices", 减轻 "lighten", 十减三 "ten minus three". In math, it is the minus verb. The word can't stand alone as an everyday verb apart from a few set phrases, and is mostly combined: 减少, 减轻, 减肥.
column4: 我最近在减肥，不吃甜的。
column5: 我最近在減肥，不吃甜的。
column6: Wǒ zuìjìn zài jiǎnféi, bù chī tián de.
column7: I'm trying to lose weight lately, so I don't eat sweet things.

column3: To reduce, decrease: it works both with an object and without. 减少浪费 "cut down waste", 人数减少了 "the numbers have gone down". 减 "decrease" plus 少 "few". It focuses on quantity or number. The opposite is 增加. With a number: 减少了一半 "reduced by half".
column6: Wǒmen yào jiǎnshǎo yòng sùliàodài.
column7: We should use fewer plastic bags.

column3: To accumulate: 积累经验 "gain experience", 积累知识, 积累财富. 积 "pile up" plus 累 "heap up". The 累 here is lěi, not lèi "tired". It is a slow, steady building up, usually of experience, knowledge or money. It can also be a noun: 经验的积累.
column4: 学习语言需要慢慢积累。
column5: 學習語言需要慢慢積累。
column6: Xuéxí yǔyán xūyào mànmàn jīlěi.
column7: Learning a language takes gradual accumulation.

column3: To scatter, disperse; spread out, for people or things in different places: 分散注意力 "distract attention", 分散投资 "spread investments", 住得很分散. 分 "divide" plus 散 "scatter". Also used as an adjective for something spread out. The opposite is 集中.
column4: 手机会分散学生的注意力。
column5: 手機會分散學生的注意力。
column6: Shǒujī huì fēnsàn xuésheng de zhùyìlì.
column7: Phones can distract students' attention.

column3: To scatter, break up, disperse: 散会 "the meeting breaks up", 散步 "go for a walk", 散开 "spread out". Read sàn here. The same character read sǎn means "loose, scattered" (散装 "sold loose"), but sàn is the verb to learn first. Everything scatters from a gathering.
column4: 会议结束了，大家都散了。
column5: 會議結束了，大家都散了。
column6: Huìyì jiéshù le, dàjiā dōu sàn le.
column7: The meeting is over and everyone has dispersed.

column3: To promote, boost: 促进发展 "promote development", 促进交流 "encourage exchanges", 互相促进 "spur each other on". 促 "urge" plus 进 "advance". The object is something good that you want to move forward, usually abstract: development, understanding, health. Formal.
column4: 运动可以促进身体健康。
column5: 運動可以促進身體健康。
column6: Yùndòng kěyǐ cùjìn shēntǐ jiànkāng.
column7: Exercise can promote good health.

column3: To move, shift, mostly in compounds: 移动 "move", 转移 "transfer", 移民 "emigrate", 移开 "move away". As a verb on its own, it takes things you can shift a little: 把桌子移一下.
column4: 请把桌子往左边移一下。
