column5: 請把桌子往左邊移一下。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhuōzi wǎng zuǒbian yí yīxià.
column7: Please move the table a little to the left.

column3: To move, shift (a thing) and "mobile": 移动电话 "mobile phone", 移动支付 "mobile payment", 慢慢移动. It is a change of position, which can be small. 移 "shift" plus 动 "move". China Mobile is named 中国移动. It may take an object: 移动桌子.
column6: Qǐng bùyào yídòng zhèxiē dōngxi.
column7: Please don't move these things.

column3: To shift, transfer: 转移注意力 "shift attention", 转移话题 "change the subject", 转移资金, 把病人转移到别的医院. 转 "turn" plus 移 "move". The thing moves from one place or state to another. The word suits both physical and abstract objects, and is somewhat formal.
column4: 他想转移话题，不谈这件事。
column5: 他想轉移話題，不談這件事。
column6: Tā xiǎng zhuǎnyí huàtí, bù tán zhè jiàn shì.
column7: He wants to change the subject and not talk about it.

column3: To turn, rotate something around a point: 转动钥匙 "turn the key", 转动方向盘 "turn the steering wheel", 眼睛转动. 转 "turn" plus 动 "move". Read zhuàn in a different word (转圈 "go round and round"), but 转动 is zhuǎndòng, with a third tone. It describes the turning of a part, not a person who changes direction (转身).
column6: Tā zhuǎndòng yàoshi, dǎkāi le mén.
column7: He turned the key and opened the door.

column3: To turn around with one's body: 转身就走 "turn and leave", 转过身来 "turn around". 转 "turn" plus 身 "body". It is a separable word: 转了一下身. It is common in stories to describe a person's quick action.
column4: 他转身就走了，什么也没说。
column5: 他轉身就走了，什麼也沒說。
column6: Tā zhuǎnshēn jiù zǒu le, shénme yě méi shuō.
column7: He turned and left without saying anything.

column3: To sway, swing, wag: 摆动手臂 "swing one's arms", 树枝在风中摆动 "branches sway in the wind", 摆动尾巴 "wag the tail". 摆 "swing" plus 动 "move". The movement goes back and forth from a fixed point, like a pendulum. The 摆 has the hand radical 扌 and often means "to place" elsewhere.
column4: 小狗高兴地摆动着尾巴。
column5: 小狗高興地擺動著尾巴。
column6: Xiǎo gǒu gāoxìng de bǎidòng zhe wěiba.
column7: The puppy wags its tail happily.

column3: To waver, shake; to undermine: 动摇信心 "shake confidence", 决不动摇 "never waver", 立场动摇. 动 "move" plus 摇 "shake". It is mostly abstract: opinions, determination and positions. It can be used of a person (他动摇了) or of something that shakes a belief.
column4: 困难没有动摇他的决心。
column5: 困難沒有動搖他的決心。
column6: Kùnnan méiyǒu dòngyáo tā de juéxīn.
column7: Difficulties did not shake his determination.

column3: To shake, wave, rock: 摇头 "shake one's head" (for "no"), 摇手 "wave one's hand", 摇晃 "sway", 摇铃. It also means "to row", as in 摇船. The 扌 is the hand radical. The shaking is done back and forth with an object or a body part.
column6: Tā yáo le yáo tóu, shuō bù zhīdào.
column7: He shook his head and said he didn't know.

column3: To fall, drop: 落雨 "rain falls", 太阳落山 "the sun sets", 落在地上 "fall to the ground", 落后 "fall behind". It is the word used for leaves, rain and the sun. Another reading, là, appears in 丢三落四 "forget this and that". The 艹 on top is the plant part, which fits leaves falling.
column6: Shùyè luò zài dì shang le.
column7: The leaves fell on the ground.

column3: Hurriedly, in haste, an adverb placed before the verb: 急忙跑过去 "hurried over", 急忙说 "hastily said". 急 "urgent" plus 忙 "busy". It describes someone quickly reacting to a sudden situation, usually in the past, not in commands.
column4: 听到哭声，她急忙跑了过去。
column5: 聽到哭聲，她急忙跑了過去。
column6: Tīngdào kūshēng, tā jímáng pǎo le guòqù.
column7: Hearing crying, she hurried over.

column3: To make the most of, not let slip: 抓紧时间 "make good use of time", 抓紧学习, 抓紧做. 抓 "grab" plus 紧 "tight", literally "grab tight". It is what you say when there is little time left, as a reminder or a command: 大家抓紧！ Also physically "to grip firmly": 抓紧扶手.
column4: 时间不多了，大家抓紧吧。
column5: 時間不多了，大家抓緊吧。
column6: Shíjiān bù duō le, dàjiā zhuājǐn ba.
column7: There isn't much time left, so let's make the most of it.

column3: As soon as possible, as quickly as one can: 尽快回复 "reply as soon as possible", 尽快完成. It comes before a verb, and is a polite request, common in emails. The 尽 is read jǐn here ("as far as possible"), not jìn. 尽快 does not set a time, which differs from 马上 "immediately".
column4: 请您尽快回复我的邮件。
column5: 請您儘快回覆我的郵件。
column6: Qǐng nín jǐnkuài huífù wǒ de yóujiàn.
column7: Please reply to my email as soon as possible.

column3: Rapid, swift: 迅速发展 "develop rapidly", 动作迅速 "quick in action", 迅速地. 迅 and 速 both mean "fast". It describes speed in a formal and written way, often for changes, reactions and spreading: 消息迅速传开. It is used before a verb or after 很.
column6: Xiāoxi xùnsù chuánbiàn le quán chéng.
column7: The news spread rapidly through the whole city.

column3: Immediately, at once, written and formal: 立即出发 "set off at once", 请立即离开. 立 "stand" plus 即 "at once". It comes before the verb and is stronger than 马上, with a note of an order or a rule. Common on notices and in news.
column4: 看到火光，他立即报了警。
column5: 看到火光，他立即報了警。
column6: Kàndào huǒguāng, tā lìjí bào le jǐng.
column7: Seeing the flames, he called the police at once.

column3: While you're at it, casually, without extra effort: 随手关门 "close the door behind you", 随手扔 "toss carelessly", 随手拿起 "pick up (casually)". 随 "follow" plus 手 "hand": what the hand does along the way. The meaning is either helpful (随手关灯 "switch off the light as you go") or careless (随手乱扔).
column6: Qǐng suíshǒu guān dēng.
column7: Please switch off the light on your way out.

column3: To take the lead, be the first to: 率先发言 "be the first to speak", 率先完成 "finish first". 率 "lead" plus 先 "first". The 率 is read shuài here. It comes before the verb and credits someone for acting before others, often in news and reports.
column4: 他率先举手回答了问题。
column5: 他率先舉手回答了問題。
column6: Tā shuàixiān jǔ shǒu huídá le wèntí.
column7: He was the first to raise a hand and answer the question.

column3: Gradually, little by little, an adverb that comes before a verb or adjective: 天渐渐黑了 "it is slowly getting dark", 渐渐习惯. It describes a change that takes place over time without notice, normally in the past or present, not in an order. It is the usual spoken pair with 逐渐.
column4: 天渐渐黑了，路上的人越来越少。
column5: 天漸漸黑了，路上的人越來越少。
column6: Tiān jiànjiàn hēi le, lù shang de rén yuè lái yuè shǎo.
column7: It was getting dark and fewer and fewer people were on the road.

column3: Gradually, the more written partner of 渐渐: 逐渐提高 "improve gradually", 逐渐增多 "gradually increase". 逐 means "one after another", 渐 "gradual". It fits reports and descriptions of trends. It cannot describe what a person does by choice, for which use 慢慢.
column4: 他的汉语水平逐渐提高了。
column5: 他的漢語水平逐漸提高了。
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ shuǐpíng zhújiàn tígāo le.
column7: His Chinese level gradually improved.

column3: Step by step, progressively: 逐步实现 "achieve step by step", 逐步改善. 逐 "one by one" plus 步 "step". The change is planned or carried out in stages, so it suits policies and projects. Compared with 逐渐, it sounds more deliberate.
column4: 我们会逐步改善这里的环境。
column5: 我們會逐步改善這裡的環境。
column6: Wǒmen huì zhúbù gǎishàn zhèlǐ de huánjìng.
column7: We will improve the environment here step by step.

column3: One after another, in succession, for people or things arriving or happening at intervals: 客人陆续到了 "guests arrived one by one", 陆续离开. It goes before the verb and describes several events spread over time. It has a plural subject. For a single action over time, use 渐渐.
column6: Kèrénmen lùxù dào le.
column7: The guests arrived one after another.

column3: Repeatedly, again and again: 一再强调 "stress repeatedly", 一再说明, 一再推迟 "put off again and again". It goes before the verb. The repeated action is often an insistence or a reminder, usually in the past or in a report. 一 means "once" and 再 "again", counting up.
column4: 老师一再提醒我们要按时交作业。
column5: 老師一再提醒我們要按時交作業。
column6: Lǎoshī yīzài tíxǐng wǒmen yào ànshí jiāo zuòyè.
column7: The teacher reminded us again and again to hand in our work on time.

column3: Over and over, repeatedly: 再三考虑 "think it over again and again", 再三感谢 "thank repeatedly", 再三强调. 再 "again" plus 三 "three": several times. It goes before the verb and stresses care or effort. Common set phrases: 再三要求, 再三推辞 "decline repeatedly".
column4: 他再三感谢我们的帮助。
column5: 他再三感謝我們的幫助。
column6: Tā zàisān gǎnxiè wǒmen de bāngzhù.
column7: He thanked us again and again for our help.

column3: One after another, in large numbers of many people or things acting in a similar way: 纷纷表示 "people said one after another", 纷纷下降 "fell one after another", 花瓣纷纷落下 "petals fall in profusion". Subject is plural. It goes before the verb and paints a picture of many doing the same.
column4: 听到这个消息，大家纷纷鼓掌。
column5: 聽到這個消息，大家紛紛鼓掌。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, dàjiā fēnfēn gǔzhǎng.
column7: On hearing the news, everyone started applauding.

column3: From then on, since then: 从此以后 "from this point on", 从此他再也没来过 "since then he has never come back". 从 "from" plus 此 "this (time)". It begins a sentence or clause and marks a turning point. It can be about the past or the future: 从此以后，我要努力学习.
column4: 他搬家以后，从此再也没有联系过。
column5: 他搬家以後，從此再也沒有聯繫過。
column6: Tā bānjiā yǐhòu, cóngcǐ zài yě méiyǒu liánxì guo.
column7: After he moved, we have never been in touch since.

column3: To hold in the arms, hug: 抱孩子 "hold a child", 抱着书 "carrying books in one's arms", 拥抱 "embrace". It also means "to harbor" a feeling: 抱希望 "hold hope", 抱怨 "complain". The hand radical 扌 plus 包 "wrap": arms wrapped round something, and 包 is also the sound.
column4: 妈妈抱着孩子走进了房间。
column5: 媽媽抱著孩子走進了房間。
column6: Māma bào zhe háizi zǒujìn le fángjiān.
column7: The mother walked into the room carrying the child.

column3: To touch, feel with the hand: 摸一摸 "give it a touch", 摸头 "pat the head", 摸黑 "feel one's way in the dark". It also means "to find out by feeling": 摸不着头脑 "can't make head nor tail of it". The hand 扌 gives the meaning; 莫 is the sound part, and the sound mō is still close to it.
column6: Bié mō nà zhī gǒu, tā huì yǎo rén.
column7: Don't touch that dog, it bites.

column3: To stick, paste, post: 贴邮票 "stick on a stamp", 贴照片, 贴海报 "put up a poster". Also "to be close to": 贴着墙 "close against the wall". The 贝 "shell, money" on the left shows up in the sense "subsidy" (补贴), and 占 is the sound part.
column4: 他在墙上贴了一张海报。
column5: 他在牆上貼了一張海報。
column6: Tā zài qiáng shang tiē le yī zhāng hǎibào.
column7: He put up a poster on the wall.

column3: To fill in, fill up: 填表 "fill in a form", 填空 "fill in the blank", 填满 "fill up". The earth radical 土 reflects its earlier sense of filling a hole with earth. The sound part 真 (zhēn) is only a rough guide now. The thing filled can be a physical gap or a blank on paper.
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhè zhāng biǎo tián yīxià.
column7: Please fill in this form.

column3: To cut, slice: 切菜 "chop vegetables", 切水果 "cut fruit", 切成片 "cut into slices". It is a kitchen word, done with a knife. There is another reading qiè in 一切 "all" and 亲切 "kind", so it's worth learning both. The measure is usually 刀 for cuts in 切一刀.
column6: Tā zhèngzài chúfáng lǐ qiē cài.
column7: She is chopping vegetables in the kitchen.

column3: To cover; to build: 盖被子 "cover oneself with a quilt", 盖章 "stamp a seal", 盖上盖子 "put the lid on"; and in the north, 盖房子 "build a house". It is also a noun, "lid". The traditional form 蓋 has the grass radical on top; the simplified form drops its lower part.
column6: Tiān lěng le, yào gài hòu bèizi.
column7: It's cold now, so use a thick quilt.

column3: To poke, pick out with a point (tiǎo): 把刺挑出来 "pick out a splinter", 挑灯 "raise a lamp". It is also in 挑战 "challenge" and 挑拨 "stir up trouble". Another reading, tiāo, means "to choose" (挑选) or "to carry on a pole". The hand radical 扌 shows an action done with the hand or a tool.
column6: Tā yòng zhēn bǎ cì tiǎo le chūlái.
column7: He picked the splinter out with a needle.

column3: To row, paddle: 划船 "row a boat", 划桨 "paddle". It is also "worth it": 划算 "good value". Read huá here. The character also stands for huà "to draw a line, to plan" in 划分 "divide", which is written 劃 in traditional characters.
column4: 周末我们去公园划船吧。
column5: 周末我們去公園划船吧。
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù gōngyuán huáchuán ba.
column7: Let's go rowing in the park at the weekend.

column3: To roll up: 卷起来 "roll up", 卷头发 "curl hair", 卷袖子 "roll up one's sleeves". Also the measure word for rolls (一卷纸 "a roll of paper"), and slang for pointless extreme competition: 内卷. The traditional form 捲 means "to roll"; 卷 as a book or exam paper is read juàn.
column4: 他把纸卷起来放进包里。
column5: 他把紙卷起來放進包裡。
column6: Tā bǎ zhǐ juǎn qǐlái fàngjìn bāo lǐ.
column7: He rolled up the paper and put it in his bag.

column3: To pull open; to pull apart; to open up a gap: 拉开门 "pull the door open", 拉开窗帘 "draw the curtains", 拉开距离 "open up a gap". 拉 "pull" plus the result 开 "apart/open". Also figuratively: 拉开序幕 "raise the curtain", for the start of an event.
column4: 她拉开窗帘，让阳光进来。
column5: 她拉開窗簾，讓陽光進來。
column6: Tā lākāi chuānglián, ràng yángguāng jìnlái.
column7: She drew the curtains to let the sunlight in.

column3: To rush, charge: 冲出去 "dash out", 往前冲 "rush forward", 冲突 "conflict". Also "to pour water on, rinse": 冲咖啡 "make coffee with hot water", 冲澡 "take a quick shower". Traditional characters keep the two apart: 衝, with 行 "road", for rushing, and 沖, with 氵 (water), for rinsing.
column4: 听到下课铃，学生们冲出了教室。
column5: 聽到下課鈴，學生們衝出了教室。
column6: Tīngdào xiàkè líng, xuéshengmen chōng chū le jiàoshì.
column7: At the bell, the students rushed out of the classroom.

column3: To pull out, draw out: 抽出一本书 "pull out a book", 抽签 "draw lots", 抽空 "find some free time", and 抽烟 "smoke". Also "to take a part from the whole": 抽时间. The 扌 hand radical hints at pulling by hand. In 抽空 and 抽时间, it means finding time out of a busy schedule.
column4: 他从书架上抽出一本书。
column5: 他從書架上抽出一本書。
column6: Tā cóng shūjià shang chōuchū yī běn shū.
column7: He pulled a book off the shelf.

column3: Thorn, sting; to prick, stab: 鱼刺 "fishbone", 刺痛 "sting with pain", 刺伤 "stab and wound". As a noun it is the sharp point of a plant or a bone. The knife radical 刂 shows the pricking. Pronounced cì with a falling tone, as in 刺激.
column6: Xiǎoxīn, zhè duǒ huā yǒu cì.
column7: Careful, this flower has thorns.

column3: To exert strength, put effort in: 使劲推 "push with all one's might", 使劲拉, 使劲儿. 使 "use" plus 劲 "strength". The 劲 is jìn here, in the sense of "force". It is a spoken, vivid word, placed before the verb: 使劲跑 "run as hard as you can".
column6: Mén tài zhòng le, nǐ děi shǐjìn tuī.
column7: The door is heavy, you have to push hard.

column3: Top, summit; to carry on the head; to push against: 山顶 "mountaintop", 头顶 "top of the head", 顶住 "hold up against", 顶着太阳 "braving the sun". It is also the measure word for hats: 一顶帽子. Also "to bump, butt": 顶了一下.
column6: Tā dài zhe yī dǐng hóng màozi.
column7: He is wearing a red hat.

column3: To avoid, dodge, hide from: mostly in compounds, 避免 "avoid", 避雨 "take shelter from rain", 避开 "step aside", 躲避 "evade". On its own it takes a concrete threat: 避雨 and 避风. The walking radical 辶 shows moving out of the way. The sound part 辟 is not very close to bì now, but it is the same sound part as in 壁 and 臂.
column4: 下雨了，我们去那边避雨吧。
column5: 下雨了，我們去那邊避雨吧。
column6: Xià yǔ le, wǒmen qù nàbiān bì yǔ ba.
column7: It's raining, let's take shelter over there.

column3: To avoid, prevent something undesirable from happening: 避免错误 "avoid mistakes", 避免浪费, 难以避免 "hard to avoid". 避 "avoid" plus 免 "escape". The object is a bad outcome. Unlike 躲, it is not about hiding from a person. It is often followed by a verb: 避免发生.
column6: Kāichē shí yào bìmiǎn jiē diànhuà.
column7: You should avoid answering the phone while driving.

column3: To shake off, get rid of, break free from: 摆脱困难 "get out of difficulty", 摆脱贫穷 "escape poverty", 摆脱烦恼. 摆 "swing" plus 脱 "come off". The object is a bad state, a burden or someone following you. It describes escaping something hard to shake.
column6: Tā xiǎng bǎituō zhè zhǒng shēnghuó.
column7: He wants to break free from this kind of life.

column3: To prevent, stop someone from doing something: 阻止他 "stop him", 阻止事故发生 "prevent an accident". 阻 "block" plus 止 "stop". It needs someone to act against something that is about to happen or is under way. Usually a person is the object: 没有人能阻止他.
column4: 没有人能阻止他去做这件事。
column5: 沒有人能阻止他去做這件事。
column6: Méiyǒu rén néng zǔzhǐ tā qù zuò zhè jiàn shì.
column7: No one can stop him from doing this.

column3: Be forced to, have no choice but: 被迫离开 "was forced to leave", 被迫放弃 "forced to give up". 被 marks the passive and 迫 means "compel". It comes before a verb and the doer is not stated. It is used when something outside forces your hand, and is more formal than 只好.
column4: 因为下大雨，比赛被迫取消了。
column5: 因為下大雨，比賽被迫取消了。
column6: Yīnwèi xià dàyǔ, bǐsài bèipò qǔxiāo le.
column7: Because of the heavy rain, the match was forced to be canceled.

column3: To bear, endure a burden, pressure or loss: 承受压力 "bear pressure", 承受痛苦, 承受不了 "can't bear it". 承 "take on" plus 受 "receive". The thing borne is heavy and often abstract or emotional, or a physical load: 承受重量. It differs from 忍受, which is gritting your teeth.
column4: 他一个人承受着很大的压力。
column5: 他一個人承受著很大的壓力。
column6: Tā yī ge rén chéngshòu zhe hěn dà de yālì.
column7: He bears a lot of pressure all by himself.

column3: To take on, bear a responsibility, cost or task: 承担责任 "take responsibility", 承担费用 "bear the cost", 承担风险 "take a risk". 承 "take on" plus 担 "carry". The 担 is dān here, "carry on the shoulder". The subject takes it on willingly or because it falls to him.
column4: 出了问题，我来承担责任。
column5: 出了問題，我來承擔責任。
column6: Chū le wèntí, wǒ lái chéngdān zérèn.
column7: If anything goes wrong, I'll take the responsibility.

column3: To meet by chance, run into; to encounter: 遇见 "meet", 遇到 "come across", 遇险 "meet danger". On its own it is rare and written, and is normally in a compound. Another sense is "to treat", as in 待遇 "treatment, pay". The 辶 shows movement, and you can think of it as "to walk into".
column6: Shēnghuó zhōng nánmiǎn huì yù kùnnan.
column7: Difficulties will inevitably come up in life.

column3: To meet, run into, come across: 遇到朋友 "run into a friend", 遇到困难 "meet with difficulty", 遇到问题. The 到 is a result: you reach the encounter. The object is a person or something unplanned, so it fits surprises and troubles. Unlike 见面, which is a meeting.
column4: 我在街上遇到了一个老朋友。
column5: 我在街上遇到了一個老朋友。
column6: Wǒ zài jiē shang yùdào le yī ge lǎo péngyou.
column7: I ran into an old friend on the street.

column3: To meet by chance, to run into someone: 遇见老师 "meet the teacher", 遇见一个人. 遇 "encounter" plus 见 "see". It is mostly used for people, and has a warm tone: 很高兴遇见你 "glad to have met you". For difficulties, use 遇到.
column4: 我昨天在地铁里遇见了老师。
column5: 我昨天在地鐵裡遇見了老師。
column6: Wǒ zuótiān zài dìtiě lǐ yùjiàn le lǎoshī.
column7: Yesterday I ran into my teacher on the subway.

column3: To stimulate, excite; stimulation: 刺激经济 "stimulate the economy", 受到刺激 "be upset". As an adjective, "exciting, thrilling": 很刺激 "very exciting", 刺激的游戏. 刺 "prick" plus 激 "stir up". It can also be harmful, as with something that hurts someone's feelings: 别刺激他.
column6: Zuò guòshānchē zhēn cìjī!
column7: Riding the roller coaster is really thrilling!

column3: Lesson (from experience) and "to lecture, scold": 吸取教训 "learn a lesson", 接受教训, 教训孩子 "give the child a talking-to". 教 "teach" plus 训 "instruct". The 训 is a neutral tone here. The noun usually refers to a bitter experience that teaches you something.
column4: 这次失败给了我们一个教训。
column5: 這次失敗給了我們一個教訓。
column6: Zhè cì shībài gěi le wǒmen yī ge jiàoxùn.
column7: This failure taught us a lesson.

column3: To complain officially, file a complaint: 投诉商店 "complain about a shop", 向经理投诉, 接到投诉 "receive a complaint". 投 "throw, submit" plus 诉 "tell". It is for a formal complaint to someone with authority, not to grumble (抱怨). Common in service settings.
column4: 我要向经理投诉这家餐厅。
column5: 我要向經理投訴這家餐廳。
column6: Wǒ yào xiàng jīnglǐ tóusù zhè jiā cāntīng.
column7: I want to make a complaint to the manager about this restaurant.

column3: Misunderstanding; to misunderstand: 这是个误会 "this is a misunderstanding", 别误会 "don't get me wrong", 误会了他的意思. 误 "mistake" plus 会 "understand". Often used to clear things up between people. It is used as both a noun and a verb.
column6: Qǐng bié wùhuì, wǒ méiyǒu shēngqì.
column7: Please don't get me wrong, I'm not angry.

column3: And, but, yet: a written connector linking two verbs, adjectives or clauses. It joins similar things (年轻而有活力 "young and energetic") or contrasts (大而不贵 "big but not expensive"). It also links a manner to a verb: 不约而同 "all at once, without agreeing". It never links nouns. Rarely used in casual talk.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu piàoliang ér piányi.
column7: This piece of clothing is pretty and cheap.

column3: But rather: it follows a negative and gives the correct statement: 不是我不想去，而是没有时间 "it's not that I don't want to go, but that I have no time". The pattern 不是……而是…… is common. 而 "but" plus 是 "be".
column4: 他不是不想去，而是没有时间。
column5: 他不是不想去，而是沒有時間。
column6: Tā bù shì bù xiǎng qù, érshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
column7: It's not that he doesn't want to go, but that he has no time.

column3: However, but, written, stronger than 但是: 他很努力，然而没有成功 "he worked hard, yet he didn't succeed". It starts the second clause, with a turn against what you expect. In speech 可是 or 但是 is more usual. The apostrophe in the pinyin marks the break between syllables.
column4: 他很努力，然而还是没有成功。
column5: 他很努力，然而還是沒有成功。
column6: Tā hěn nǔlì, rán'ér háishi méiyǒu chénggōng.
column7: He worked hard, but he still didn't succeed.

column3: But, yet, however, placed after the subject and before the verb: 他很想去，却没有时间 "he wanted to go, but had no time". It is milder than 但是 and shows an unexpected turn. It cannot start a clause; it goes inside it, often with 可是 or 但是: 可是他却不来.
column4: 我等了他很久，他却没来。
column5: 我等了他很久，他卻沒來。
column6: Wǒ děng le tā hěn jiǔ, tā què méi lái.
column7: I waited for him for a long time, but he didn't come.

column3: Otherwise, or else: 快走，否则要迟到了 "hurry, or you'll be late". It starts the second clause and states the bad result if the first doesn't happen. Written and slightly formal. 否 "not" plus 则 "then". In speech 不然 is more usual.
column4: 快点走，否则我们要迟到了。
column5: 快點走，否則我們要遲到了。
column6: Kuài diǎn zǒu, fǒuzé wǒmen yào chídào le.
column7: Hurry up, otherwise we will be late.

column3: Otherwise, or else: the spoken form of 否则: 快走吧，不然要迟到了. It starts the second clause. Also "not so": 不然，他不会这样 (written). And as a suggestion: 不然我们去看电影吧 "how about we see a film?".
column4: 早点睡吧，不然明天起不来。
column5: 早點睡吧，不然明天起不來。
column6: Zǎodiǎn shuì ba, bùrán míngtiān qǐ bu lái.
column7: Go to bed early, or you won't be able to get up tomorrow.

column3: No matter (who, what, how): it comes with a question word or a choice: 不管谁来 "no matter who comes", 不管多难 "however hard", 不管你去不去. The main clause then uses 都 or 也: 不管怎样，我都支持你. It is spoken. 无论 is the written equivalent.
column4: 不管多难，我都要试一试。
column5: 不管多難，我都要試一試。
column6: Bùguǎn duō nán, wǒ dōu yào shì yi shì.
column7: No matter how hard it is, I'll give it a try.

column3: No matter (what/how), the written partner of 不管: 无论发生什么 "whatever happens", 无论如何 "in any case". It comes with a question word or a choice, and the main clause uses 都 or 也. 无 "not" plus 论 "discuss".
column4: 无论天气怎么样，我们都去。
column5: 無論天氣怎麼樣，我們都去。
column6: Wúlùn tiānqì zěnmeyàng, wǒmen dōu qù.
column7: Whatever the weather, we are going.

column3: Even if, even though: 哪怕下雨，我也要去 "even if it rains, I'll still go". The second clause normally has 也 or 都. 哪 "which" plus 怕 "fear": "no matter what you fear". The condition can be unlikely, and the conclusion stays the same.
column6: Nǎpà xià dàyǔ, wǒ yě yào qù.
column7: Even if it rains heavily, I still want to go.

column3: Just in case, if by any chance: 万一下雨怎么办？ "what if it rains?", 万一出事. It introduces an unlikely event and the main clause says what to do. As a noun, it means "the unlikely event": 以防万一 "just in case". 万 "ten thousand" plus 一 "one", so one chance in ten thousand.
column6: Dài shàng sǎn ba, wànyī xià yǔ ne.
column7: Take an umbrella, just in case it rains.

column3: If, supposing, a written conditional: 假如我是你 "if I were you", 假如明天下雨. It sets up an imaginary or unlikely condition. 假 "suppose" plus 如 "as if". It is more formal than 如果, and the main clause may begin with 就 or 那么.
column4: 假如我是你，我就不会这样做。
column5: 假如我是你，我就不會這樣做。
column6: Jiǎrú wǒ shì nǐ, wǒ jiù bù huì zhèyàng zuò.
column7: If I were you, I wouldn't do it like that.

column3: Already; both... and..: in the pattern 既……又…… "both... and..." and in 既然 "since". 既聪明又努力 "both smart and hard-working". It is written and almost never on its own. The picture is a person turned away from a bowl of food, finished eating, which is where "already" comes from.
column6: Tā jì cōngmíng yòu nǔlì.
column7: She is both clever and hardworking.

column3: Since, now that: it states a fact that is already settled and draws a conclusion: 既然你来了，就坐一会儿吧 "since you're here, sit for a while". The second clause often has 就 or 那么. It differs from 因为, which gives a cause. 既然 shows what is accepted.
column4: 既然你累了，就早点休息吧。
column5: 既然你累了，就早點休息吧。
column6: Jìrán nǐ lèi le, jiù zǎodiǎn xiūxi ba.
column7: Since you are tired, get some rest early.

column3: And, as well as, written, joining nouns or phrases and putting the main item first: 书、杂志以及报纸 "books, magazines and newspapers". Not for verbs or clauses. In a list the final item takes 以及. It is less common in speech, where 和 is used.
column4: 桌子上有书、笔以及一些水果。
column5: 桌子上有書、筆以及一些水果。
column6: Zhuōzi shang yǒu shū, bǐ yǐjí yīxiē shuǐguǒ.
column7: On the table there are books, pens and some fruit.

column3: Besides, in addition: it starts a sentence and adds a further point: 此外，我还想说…… 此 "this" plus 外 "outside": "outside of this". It is written, often used in reports and essays to continue a list. In speech, 另外 is the usual word.
column4: 他会说英语，此外还会说日语。
column5: 他會說英語，此外還會說日語。
column6: Tā huì shuō Yīngyǔ, cǐwài hái huì shuō Rìyǔ.
column7: He speaks English, and besides that he speaks Japanese.

column3: This: a written word, rarely alone but in set phrases: 此时 "at this time", 此外 "besides", 因此 "for this reason", 从此 "from then on", 由此可见. The character has the foot 止 on the left, and the idea is "the place where one stops": here.
column4: 此时此刻，他心里很高兴。
column5: 此時此刻，他心裡很高興。
column6: Cǐshí cǐkè, tā xīnli hěn gāoxìng.
column7: At this very moment he is very happy.

column3: So, thereupon, and then: it links two events where the second follows from the first: 天黑了，于是我们回家了 "it got dark, so we went home". It begins the second clause. The result is a natural consequence or the next step, not a logical conclusion like 所以.
column4: 天黑了，于是我们回家了。
column5: 天黑了，於是我們回家了。
column6: Tiān hēi le, yúshì wǒmen huí jiā le.
column7: It got dark, so we went home.

column3: Law, method, way: 方法 "method", 办法 "way", 法律 "law", 法语 "French". On its own it is mostly "law": 学法 "study law", 法不责众. The water 氵 on the left and 去 "go" on the right suggest a course followed.
column6: Wǒ gēge zài dàxué xué fǎ.
column7: My older brother studies law at university.

column3: Judge in a court: 法官判决 "the judge's ruling", 当法官. 法 "law" plus 官 "official". The measure word is 位 or 名. A judge speaks in court: 法官说. A 律师 "lawyer" argues a case before the judge.
column4: 法官宣布了最后的结果。
column5: 法官宣布了最後的結果。
column6: Fǎguān xuānbù le zuìhòu de jiéguǒ.
column7: The judge announced the final result.

column3: Law, the body of rules a state enforces: 遵守法律 "obey the law", 学法律 "study law", 违反法律 "break the law", 法律规定 "the law stipulates". 法 "law" plus 律 "rule", two near-synonyms. Used for law as a whole and for particular laws. Pinyin is stored with v for ü: lv4.
column4: 每个人都应该遵守法律。
column5: 每個人都應該遵守法律。
column6: Měi ge rén dōu yīnggāi zūnshǒu fǎlǜ.
column7: Everyone should obey the law.

column3: Court, courthouse: 去法院 "go to court", 最高法院 "the Supreme Court", 起诉到法院. 法 "law" plus 院 "institution/courtyard". It is the institution that holds trials, and also the building. The people in it include 法官 "judge".
column4: 这个案子明天在法院开庭。
column5: 這個案子明天在法院開庭。
column6: Zhège ànzi míngtiān zài fǎyuàn kāitíng.
column7: This case will be heard in court tomorrow.

column3: Rule, regulation for a game, a system or a traffic situation: 游戏规则 "the rules of the game", 交通规则 "traffic rules", 遵守规则. Also "regular" as an adjective: 不规则 "irregular". 规 "compass, standard" plus 则 "rule". Stronger and more formal than 规矩, which is about customary behavior.
column6: Bǐsài yǒu zìjǐ de guīzé.
column7: The competition has its own rules.

column3: Regular pattern; law (of nature): 自然规律 "laws of nature", 找规律 "find the pattern", 生活有规律 "a regular lifestyle". Also an adjective: 作息很规律 "keep regular hours". 规 "standard" plus 律 "rule". It describes something you discover, not something imposed (that is 规则).
column6: Tā de shēnghuó hěn yǒu guīlǜ.
column7: He lives a very regular life.

column3: Discipline, the rules a group has to follow: 遵守纪律 "keep to discipline", 课堂纪律 "classroom discipline", 纪律严明 "strict discipline". 纪 "record, order" plus 律 "rule". It is used for schools, armies and workplaces. The thread radical 纟 in 纪 is from the idea of putting threads in order.
column6: Xuésheng yào zūnshǒu kètáng jìlǜ.
column7: Students must keep to classroom discipline.

column3: Principle, a basic standard: 原则上 "in principle", 有原则 "have principles", 坚持原则 "stick to principles", 违反原则. 原 "origin" plus 则 "rule". 原则上 often introduces a general rule before an exception: 原则上可以，但是…… Fits a person's morals and an organization's rules.
column4: 在原则问题上，他从不让步。
column5: 在原則問題上，他從不讓步。
column6: Zài yuánzé wèntí shang, tā cóng bù ràngbù.
column7: On matters of principle, he never gives way.

column3: To forbid, prohibit: 禁止吸烟 "no smoking", 禁止入内 "no entry", 严禁. It appears on signs and in rules, and sounds firm. 禁 "forbid" plus 止 "stop". The 禁 here is read jìn; in 禁不住 "cannot help" it is jīn.
column6: Zhèlǐ jìnzhǐ tíngchē.
column7: Parking is not allowed here.

column3: To restrict, limit and "restriction, limit": 限制人数 "limit the number of people", 没有限制 "no limit", 年龄限制 "age limit". 限 "boundary" plus 制 "control". The restriction is set by rules or circumstances. It differs from 禁止 as it allows within limits.
column6: Zhège yóuxì yǒu niánlíng xiànzhì.
column7: This game has an age limit.

column3: Policy, guiding principle, from the political vocabulary: 基本方针 "basic policy", 工作方针, 制定方针. 方 "direction" plus 针 "needle", as in a compass needle. It is a broad line set by a government or organization to follow, bigger than a particular step (措施).
column4: 国家制定了新的教育方针。
column5: 國家制定了新的教育方針。
column6: Guójiā zhìdìng le xīn de jiàoyù fāngzhēn.
column7: The country has drawn up a new education policy.

column3: Measure, step taken to deal with a problem: 采取措施 "take measures", 安全措施 "safety measures", 有效的措施. 措 "handle" plus 施 "carry out". Often with 采取. Unlike 方针, this is a concrete action. Counted by 项: 一项措施.
column4: 政府采取了一些新的措施。
column5: 政府採取了一些新的措施。
column6: Zhèngfǔ cǎiqǔ le yīxiē xīn de cuòshī.
column7: The government has taken some new measures.

column3: To work out, draw up a plan, rule or law: 制订计划 "draw up a plan", 制订规则, 制订方案. 制 "make" plus 订 "set". The object is a document or plan, and it sounds a bit formal. It is nearly the same as 制定, which is the other form.
column4: 我们一起制订了一个学习计划。
column5: 我們一起制訂了一個學習計劃。
column6: Wǒmen yīqǐ zhìdìng le yī ge xuéxí jìhuà.
column7: Together we drew up a study plan.

column3: Government: 中国政府 "the Chinese government", 地方政府 "local government", 政府部门. 政 "government affairs" plus 府 "office". It names the executive body that governs, at any level. The measure word is 个 if needed. Not the same as 国家 "the nation".
column4: 政府决定增加学校的数量。
column5: 政府決定增加學校的數量。
column6: Zhèngfǔ juédìng zēngjiā xuéxiào de shùliàng.
column7: The government decided to increase the number of schools.

column3: Politics; political: 政治家 "politician", 关心政治 "take an interest in politics", 政治问题. 政 "government" plus 治 "manage". It can be a noun or an adjective before a noun, and 政治 is also a school subject. Sometimes it means "ideology" or "political position".
column6: Tā duì zhèngzhì hěn gǎn xìngqù.
column7: He is very interested in politics.

column3: Premier, prime minister, head of a government: 国务院总理 "the Premier of the State Council", 德国总理. 总 "overall" plus 理 "manage". In China the premier heads the government, below the president. Used in titles and news.
column4: 新总理今天发表了讲话。
column5: 新總理今天發表了講話。
column6: Xīn zǒnglǐ jīntiān fābiǎo le jiǎnghuà.
column7: The new prime minister gave a speech today.

column3: President of a republic: 美国总统 "the US president", 总统选举 "presidential election". 总 "overall" plus 统 "lead". It is used for the head of state of countries such as the United States and Taiwan. In the PRC, the head of state is called 主席.
column4: 美国总统明天要访问中国。
column5: 美國總統明天要訪問中國。
column6: Měiguó zǒngtǒng míngtiān yào fǎngwèn Zhōngguó.
column7: The American president will visit China tomorrow.

column3: Official, officer in government: 当官 "hold office", 官员 "official", 官僚, 军官 "military officer", 警官. On its own it means a government post-holder, in the old sense a mandarin. The 宀 roof on top shows a public building, an office, where the official worked.
column6: Tā xiǎng dāng guān, dànshì wǒ bù xiǎng.
column7: He wants to be an official, but I don't.

column3: Official (from the authorities): 官方网站 "official website", 官方消息 "official news", 官方语言 "official language". 官 "authority" plus 方 "side". The opposite is 民间 "popular, unofficial". It is the word to use for approved sources and statements.
column4: 请看官方网站上的通知。
column5: 請看官方網站上的通知。
column6: Qǐng kàn guānfāng wǎngzhàn shang de tōngzhī.
column7: Please look at the notice on the official website.

column3: The public, the masses or "popular": 大众媒体 "mass media", 大众文化 "popular culture", 大众化 "popularized". 大 "big" plus 众 "crowd" (the character shows three people). It names ordinary people as a whole. It is also the Chinese name of Volkswagen: 大众汽车.
column4: 这是一家受大众喜爱的饭店。
column5: 這是一家受大眾喜愛的飯店。
column6: Zhè shì yī jiā shòu dàzhòng xǐ'ài de fàndiàn.
column7: This is a restaurant loved by the public.

column3: To unify; unified, standardized: 统一思想 "unify thinking", 统一标准 "standard", 统一管理 "unified management", 统一中国. 统 "unite" plus 一 "one". As a verb, it combines several into one; as an adjective, it means all the same, uniform: 统一的制服.
column4: 同学们穿着统一的校服。
column5: 同學們穿著統一的校服。
column6: Tóngxuémen chuān zhe tǒngyī de xiàofú.
column7: The students are wearing the same school uniform.

column3: King: 国王 "king", 王子 "prince", 王后 "queen", and also a very common surname. In compounds it means "best of its kind": 球王 "king of football", 歌王. The character looks like 玉 "jade" without its dot.
column6: Tā shì zhège guójiā de wáng.
column7: He is the king of this country.

column3: Diplomat: 外 "foreign" plus 交 "relations" gives 外交 "foreign affairs, diplomacy", and 官 "official" completes it. 当外交官 "become a diplomat", 一名外交官. It is a job, and all diplomats work for a government.
column4: 她的爸爸是一名外交官。
column5: 她的爸爸是一名外交官。
column6: Tā de bàba shì yī míng wàijiāoguān.
column7: Her father is a diplomat.

column3: Right, entitlement: 有权利 "have the right", 享有权利 "enjoy rights", 公民的权利 "citizens' rights", 放弃权利. 权 "power" plus 利 "benefit". It is the thing the law or society gives you the freedom to do. Paired with 义务 "duty": 权利和义务.
column4: 每个人都有受教育的权利。
column5: 每個人都有受教育的權利。
column6: Měi ge rén dōu yǒu shòu jiàoyù de quánlì.
column7: Everyone has the right to be educated.

column3: Duty, obligation, and also "unpaid, voluntary": 尽义务 "do one's duty", 义务教育 "compulsory education", 义务劳动 "voluntary work". 义 "righteousness" plus 务 "task". It goes together with 权利: 权利和义务. The measure word is 项: 一项义务.
column4: 纳税是每个公民的义务。
column5: 納稅是每個公民的義務。
column6: Nàshuì shì měi ge gōngmín de yìwù.
column7: Paying tax is every citizen's duty.

column3: To fight, battle; combat: 参加战斗 "take part in combat", 战斗机 "fighter plane", 战斗英雄. 战 "war" plus 斗 "fight". The word is about armed combat, but can be used figuratively for any hard struggle.
column4: 战士们勇敢地投入了战斗。
column5: 戰士們勇敢地投入了戰鬥。
column6: Zhànshìmen yǒnggǎn de tóurù le zhàndòu.
column7: The soldiers bravely threw themselves into the battle.

column3: War: 发动战争 "start a war", 世界大战 "world war", 反对战争 "oppose war", 战争结束. 战 "war" plus 争 "fight". It names a war as a historical or political event, on a larger scale than 战斗, which is one fight. The measure word is 场: 一场战争.
column4: 战争给人们带来了很多痛苦。
column5: 戰爭給人們帶來了很多痛苦。
column6: Zhànzhēng gěi rénmen dàilái le hěn duō tòngkǔ.
column7: War brought people a lot of suffering.

column3: Soldier, fighter: 解放军战士 "a soldier of the PLA", 一名战士, 勇敢的战士. 战 "war" plus 士 "man, soldier". It is a respectful word, used for ordinary servicemen or for people who fight for a cause: 和平战士. In the plain sense, a soldier is also 士兵.
column4: 这位战士受了很重的伤。
column5: 這位戰士受了很重的傷。
column6: Zhè wèi zhànshì shòu le hěn zhòng de shāng.
column7: This soldier was badly wounded.

column3: Soldier: 当兵 "join the army", 士兵 "soldier", 步兵 "infantry", 兵马. Also a chess piece, a pawn, in Chinese chess. In the picture, two hands hold up an axe: a person bearing arms. 当兵 is the spoken phrase for doing military service.
column6: Tā shíbā suì jiù qù dāng bīng le.
column7: He joined the army at eighteen.

column3: Enemy: 战胜敌人 "defeat the enemy", 共同的敌人 "common enemy", 把他当作敌人. 敌 "opponent" plus 人 "person". It can be a country, a person or a thing that harms you (健康的敌人 "an enemy of health"). The opposite is 朋友.
column6: Áoyè shì jiànkāng de dírén.
column7: Staying up late is the enemy of health.

column3: To conquer: 征服世界 "conquer the world", 征服敌人, 被征服. 征 "march against" plus 服 "submit". It is also used figuratively, 征服观众 "win over the audience" and 征服高山 "conquer a mountain". The 彳 on the left of 征 shows walking.
column4: 他成功地征服了这座高山。
column5: 他成功地征服了這座高山。
column6: Tā chénggōng de zhēngfú le zhè zuò gāoshān.
column7: He successfully conquered this high mountain.

column3: To command, direct; conductor: 指挥交通 "direct traffic", 指挥部队, 乐队指挥 "orchestra conductor". As a noun, it is the person who commands, or the music conductor. 指 "point" plus 挥 "wave". The hand radical 扌 appears in both, a hint at signaling with the hand.
column6: Jǐngchá zhèngzài zhǐhuī jiāotōng.
column7: The police officer is directing the traffic.

column3: To defeat, overcome: 战胜对手 "beat an opponent", 战胜困难 "overcome difficulties", 战胜疾病. 战 "fight" plus 胜 "win". It can be used for war or sport, but often in a figurative sense, for overcoming something hard. The object follows directly.
column4: 他战胜了病魔，重新站了起来。
column5: 他戰勝了病魔，重新站了起來。
column6: Tā zhànshèng le bìngmó, chóngxīn zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: He overcame his illness and stood up again.

column3: To defeat, beat an opponent: 打败对手 "beat a rival", 打败敌人, 被打败. 打 "hit" plus the result 败 "be beaten". Used for games, battles and competitions. In a result complement you can make it potential: 打得败 "can beat", 打不败 "can't beat".
column6: Wǒmen duì dǎbài le duìshǒu.
column7: Our team beat the opponents.

column3: To lose, be defeated; to fail: 失败 "fail", 战败 "lose a war", 打败 "defeat", 败给 "lose to". On its own it is a literary word, used as a verb for losing: 败在……手下. It also means "to decay": 败坏.
column4: 这场比赛我们败给了对手。
column5: 這場比賽我們敗給了對手。
column6: Zhè chǎng bǐsài wǒmen bài gěi le duìshǒu.
column7: We lost this match to our opponents.

column3: Soldier, an ordinary member of the armed forces: 一名士兵 "a soldier", 年轻的士兵. 士 "soldier, man" plus 兵 "troops". Used for an enlisted person of any army. It is a plain, factual word, unlike 战士, which has a respectful tone.
column4: 士兵们在广场上整齐地站着。
column5: 士兵們在廣場上整齊地站著。
column6: Shìbīngmen zài guǎngchǎng shang zhěngqí de zhàn zhe.
column7: The soldiers stand in neat rows on the square.

column3: Heroic, brave: 英勇作战 "fight heroically", 英勇的战士 "a gallant soldier", 英勇牺牲 "die a hero's death". 英 "outstanding" plus 勇 "brave". A praising and slightly literary word for bravery in danger, used in speeches, stories and news.
column4: 消防员英勇地冲进了火场。
column5: 消防員英勇地衝進了火場。
column6: Xiāofángyuán yīngyǒng de chōngjìn le huǒchǎng.
column7: The firefighters heroically rushed into the fire.

column3: Regarding, as for, introducing the topic or person that an opinion concerns: 对于这件事，我没有意见 "as for this matter, I have no objection", 对于学生来说. It is used before the subject or after it, and the thing following is the subject of the attitude. Unlike 关于, it needs a viewpoint or a reaction.
column4: 对于这件事，我没有意见。
column5: 對於這件事，我沒有意見。
column6: Duìyú zhè jiàn shì, wǒ méiyǒu yìjiàn.
column7: As for this matter, I have no objection.

column3: About, concerning: 关于历史的书 "a book about history", 关于这个问题. It names the topic of a text, talk or discussion. A phrase with 关于 becomes a modifier with 的, or starts a sentence. Unlike 对于, it is purely about the subject matter, not an attitude.
column4: 我买了一本关于中国历史的书。
column5: 我買了一本關於中國歷史的書。
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī běn guānyú Zhōngguó lìshǐ de shū.
column7: I bought a book about Chinese history.

column3: To be aimed at, target; in response to: 针对问题 "target the problem", 针对儿童 "aimed at children", 针对性 "targeted". 针 "needle" plus 对 "face": aimed like a needle. Often used for plans and statements that respond to a particular issue.
column4: 这个活动是针对小学生的。
column5: 這個活動是針對小學生的。
column6: Zhège huódòng shì zhēnduì xiǎoxuéshēng de.
column7: This activity is aimed at primary school students.

column3: According to, based on: 根据报道 "according to reports", 根据情况 "depending on the situation". 根 "root" plus 据 "basis". It starts a sentence, or comes before a verb. As a noun it is "basis, grounds": 有根据 "well-founded", 没有根据.
column4: 根据天气预报，明天有雨。
column5: 根據天氣預報，明天有雨。
column6: Gēnjù tiānqì yùbào, míngtiān yǒu yǔ.
column7: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.

column3: As, in the capacity of: 作为学生 "as a student", 作为朋友. It starts a sentence and then states what follows from a role. Also "to act as": 作为礼物 "as a gift". The reading is wéi, not wèi. As a noun it means "achievement": 有作为 "make something of oneself".
column4: 作为学生，你应该认真学习。
column5: 作為學生，你應該認真學習。
column6: Zuòwéi xuésheng, nǐ yīnggāi rènzhēn xuéxí.
column7: As a student, you should study seriously.

column3: Lies in, depends on: 关键在于努力 "the key lies in effort", 区别在于…… "the difference lies in...". It points to the reason or point of the matter and appears in written style. 在 "be at" plus 于 "in". It links a subject to what it consists of or depends on.
column6: Chénggōng de guānjiàn zàiyú jiānchí.
column7: The key to success lies in persistence.

column3: To do for someone, instead of: 替我买票 "buy a ticket for me", 替他高兴 "be happy for him", 替人看孩子. As a coverb, it marks the person on whose behalf you act. Also a verb "to replace": 替换. The 替 is two people (夫夫) above 日, which shows one taking another's place.
column6: Nǐ néng tì wǒ mǎi yī zhāng piào ma?
column7: Can you buy a ticket for me?

column3: From, since (written) and "self": 来自 "come from", 自古 "since ancient times", 自己 "oneself", 自从 "since". On its own it appears before a place or time: 自北京来 "from Beijing". The character was a picture of a nose, and people pointed at their nose to say "I".
column6: Zhè wèi kèrén zì Běijīng lái.
column7: This guest has come from Beijing.

column3: To face, be confronted with: 面临困难 "face difficulties", 面临危险, 面临选择. 面 "face" plus 临 "arrive at". The thing faced is a challenge, danger or decision. The subject is a person, group or country, and the sentence is formal.
column4: 我们面临着很大的困难。
column5: 我們面臨著很大的困難。
column6: Wǒmen miànlín zhe hěn dà de kùnnan.
column7: We are facing great difficulties.

column3: To be located at: 位于北京 "is located in Beijing", 位于河边. 位 "position" plus 于 "at". A written way to say where a place is, in descriptions and textbooks, followed by the place. The subject is a building, city or region, not a person.
column6: Wǒ jiā wèiyú shì zhōngxīn.
column7: My home is in the city center.

column3: To be in (a state or position): 处于领先地位 "be in the lead", 处于危险中 "be in danger", 处于困难之中. 处 "be in" plus 于 "at". The 处 is read chǔ here. The word describes a situation, usually abstract, and is formal.
column4: 他现在处于很危险的状态。
column5: 他現在處於很危險的狀態。
column6: Tā xiànzài chǔyú hěn wēixiǎn de zhuàngtài.
column7: He is in a very dangerous state now.

column3: To replace, take the place of: 代替他 "take his place", 没有东西能代替它. 代 "stand in for" plus 替 "substitute". The thing that takes the place comes first and the thing replaced is the object: 机器代替人.
column4: 没有人能代替他的位置。
column5: 沒有人能代替他的位置。
column6: Méiyǒu rén néng dàitì tā de wèizhi.
column7: No one can take his place.

column3: To substitute for, replace: 替代品 "a substitute", 被……替代 "be replaced by". It is similar to 代替 but is more about one thing taking the place of another over time, especially technology: 新技术替代旧技术.
column4: 电子书正在慢慢替代纸质书。
column5: 電子書正在慢慢替代紙質書。
column6: Diànzǐshū zhèngzài mànmàn tìdài zhǐzhì shū.
column7: E-books are slowly replacing paper books.

column3: To rely on, depend on: 依靠自己 "rely on oneself", 依靠别人, 无依无靠 "have no one to rely on". 依 and 靠 both mean "lean on". As a noun it means "support": 他是我们的依靠. Used for people, a tool or an effort.
column6: Wǒmen zhǐ néng yīkào zìjǐ.
column7: We can only rely on ourselves.

column3: Source, origin: 消息来源 "the source of the news", 经济来源 "source of income", 来源于 "come from". 来 "come" plus 源 "spring". It is the place from which something comes. As a verb with 于: 知识来源于实践.
column4: 这个消息的来源是什么？
column5: 這個消息的來源是什麼？
column6: Zhège xiāoxi de láiyuán shì shénme?
column7: What is the source of this news?

column3: Structure: 房屋结构 "the structure of a building", 句子结构 "sentence structure", 结构复杂. 结 "tie" plus 构 "build". Describes how parts are put together, in buildings, texts, society or the body. Also a pattern of parts in a whole.
column4: 这个句子的结构很复杂。
column5: 這個句子的結構很複雜。
column6: Zhège jùzi de jiégòu hěn fùzá.
column7: This sentence has a complicated structure.

column3: To constitute, make up, form: 构成威胁 "pose a threat", 由……构成 "be made up of", 构成部分. 构 "build" plus 成 "become". The common pattern is 由 A 构成: 水由氢和氧构成. Also "to constitute (a crime)": 构成犯罪.
column6: Shuǐ shì yóu qīng hé yǎng gòuchéng de.
column7: Water is made up of hydrogen and oxygen.

column3: Structure, construction, how something is built, esp. a machine or organ: 机器的构造 "the machine's structure", 身体构造. 构 "build" plus 造 "make". More physical than 结构 and often used for technical things. Can also be a verb, "to construct" (a sentence, a theory).
column4: 这台机器的构造很简单。
column5: 這台機器的構造很簡單。
column6: Zhè tái jīqì de gòuzào hěn jiǎndān.
column7: This machine is simply built.

column3: To tie, fasten: 系鞋带 "tie shoelaces", 系领带 "put on a tie", 系安全带 "fasten the seat belt". In this sense 系 is read jì and its traditional form is 繫. The same character is read xì in 关系 "relationship" and 系统 "system", which come from a different traditional character, 係/系.
column4: 上车以后，请系好安全带。
column5: 上車以後，請繫好安全帶。
column6: Shàng chē yǐhòu, qǐng jì hǎo ānquándài.
column7: After getting in the car, please fasten your seat belt.

column3: Knot; to tie, form: 打结 "tie a knot", 结婚 "marry", 结果 "result", 结束 "end", 结账 "pay the bill". As a word on its own it means a knot or "to bear fruit": 结果子. The thread radical 纟 fits the sense of tying. In 结实 "sturdy" it is jiē.
column4: 他在绳子上打了一个结。
column5: 他在繩子上打了一個結。
column6: Tā zài shéngzi shang dǎ le yī ge jié.
column7: He tied a knot in the rope.

column3: Order, sequence: 按顺序 "in order", 排顺序 "put in order", 先后顺序 "order of precedence", 打乱顺序 "mix up the order". 顺 "follow" plus 序 "sequence". It names the arrangement of items in a row, in time or in position.
column4: 请按顺序排队，不要着急。
column5: 請按順序排隊，不要著急。
column6: Qǐng àn shùnxù páiduì, bùyào zháojí.
column7: Please line up in order and don't be impatient.

column3: To arrange, line up in order: 排列整齐 "neatly arranged", 按顺序排列 "arrange in order", 排列组合 "permutations and combinations" (math). 排 "line up" plus 列 "row". The things are set out in a fixed order or pattern.
column4: 请把这些词按顺序排列。
column5: 請把這些詞按順序排列。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhèxiē cí àn shùnxù páiliè.
column7: Please arrange these words in order.

column3: To be distributed, spread out; distribution: 分布在 "spread over", 分布范围 "range", 人口分布 "population distribution". 分 "divide" plus 布 "spread". It names how things are located over an area, as in geography or statistics.
column4: 大熊猫主要分布在四川。
column5: 大熊貓主要分佈在四川。
column6: Dàxióngmāo zhǔyào fēnbù zài Sìchuān.
column7: Giant pandas live mainly in Sichuan.

column3: To divide into: 分为三部分 "divided into three parts", 分为两组. 分 "divide" plus 为 "become" (here wéi). A structure for describing parts: A 分为 B 和 C. It is common in written descriptions.
column6: Zhè běn shū fēnwéi sān ge bùfen.
column7: This book is divided into three parts.

column3: To be listed as, classified as: 列为重点 "listed as a priority", 被列为世界遗产 "inscribed as a World Heritage site". 列 "list" plus 为 "as" (wéi). It appears in formal news and notices, often with 被.
column4: 这座古城被列为世界文化遗产。
column5: 這座古城被列為世界文化遺產。
column6: Zhè zuò gǔchéng bèi lièwéi shìjiè wénhuà yíchǎn.
column7: This ancient city is listed as a World Cultural Heritage site.

column3: To include in a list: 列入名单 "put on the list", 列入计划 "include in the plan". 列 "list" plus 入 "enter". The list is a formal one, such as a roll, a schedule or a plan.
column4: 他的名字被列入了名单。
column5: 他的名字被列入了名單。
column6: Tā de míngzi bèi lièrù le míngdān.
column7: His name was put on the list.

column3: Row, series; to list: as a measure word for trains: 一列火车 "a train", 一列队伍 "a column of people". 列出 "list out", 列表 "list", 排列 "arrange". In a data table, 列 is the column. The knife radical 刂 suggests cutting things into lines.
column4: 一列火车从远处开了过来。
column5: 一列火車從遠處開了過來。
column6: Yī liè huǒchē cóng yuǎnchù kāi le guòlái.
column7: A train came from the distance.

column3: Kind, type, variety: 种类很多 "many kinds", 不同种类 "different types", 增加种类. 种 "kind" plus 类 "category". It names how many sorts there are, rather than a single type, and is used for goods, animals, plants.
column4: 这家商店的水果种类很多。
column5: 這家商店的水果種類很多。
column6: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn de shuǐguǒ zhǒnglèi hěn duō.
column7: This shop has many kinds of fruit.

column3: Type, kind: 不同类型 "different types", 电影类型 "film genre" and 数据类型 "data type". 类 "category" plus 型 "model, pattern". It names a group that shares features, and is slightly more formal than 种. The measure word is 种: 这种类型.
column4: 你喜欢哪种类型的电影？
column5: 你喜歡哪種類型的電影？
column6: Nǐ xǐhuan nǎ zhǒng lèixíng de diànyǐng?
column7: What type of film do you like?

column3: Series, set: 系列活动 "a series of events", 系列产品 "a product line", 一系列问题 "a series of questions". 系 "link" plus 列 "row". In 一系列, it works as a modifier before a noun and means "a whole string of". The 系 here is read xì.
column4: 学校举办了一系列文化活动。
column5: 學校舉辦了一系列文化活動。
column6: Xuéxiào jǔbàn le yī xìliè wénhuà huódòng.
column7: The school held a series of cultural activities.

column3: To lead to, cause (a bad result): 导致事故 "lead to an accident", 导致失败. 导 "lead" plus 致 "bring about". The result is almost always negative, so it is the word for cause and effect with bad effects. The cause is the subject: 大雨导致了交通堵塞.
column4: 大雨导致了严重的交通堵塞。
column5: 大雨導致了嚴重的交通堵塞。
column6: Dàyǔ dǎozhì le yánzhòng de jiāotōng dǔsè.
column7: The heavy rain led to serious traffic jams.

column3: To spur, prompt (someone to do something): 促使他改变 "prompted him to change". 促 "urge" plus 使 "cause". After the object comes a verb: 这件事促使我努力学习. The cause is the subject. The tone is formal and the effect usually active.
column4: 这次失败促使他更加努力。
column5: 這次失敗促使他更加努力。
column6: Zhè cì shībài cùshǐ tā gèngjiā nǔlì.
column7: This failure spurred him to work even harder.

column3: To cause, arouse: 引起注意 "attract attention", 引起兴趣 "arouse interest", 引起误会 "cause a misunderstanding". 引 "draw" plus 起 "rise". The object is a reaction, feeling or problem. Both good and bad outcomes can be caused. The cause is the subject.
column4: 他的话引起了大家的注意。
column5: 他的話引起了大家的注意。
column6: Tā de huà yǐnqǐ le dàjiā de zhùyì.
column7: His words attracted everyone's attention.

column3: To guide, lead a person's thinking or behavior: 引导学生 "guide students", 引导孩子思考. 引 "lead" plus 导 "guide". The guidance is gentle and indirect, from a teacher or parent. It differs from 带领, which is physically leading a group.
column4: 老师引导学生自己找答案。
column5: 老師引導學生自己找答案。
column6: Lǎoshī yǐndǎo xuésheng zìjǐ zhǎo dá'àn.
column7: The teacher guides students to find the answers themselves.

column3: To bring in, introduce from outside: 引进技术 "import technology", 引进人才 "recruit talent", 引进外资 "bring in foreign capital". 引 "draw" plus 进 "enter". The object is technology, equipment, ideas or experts. It is a formal word used for institutions.
column4: 公司从国外引进了新设备。
column5: 公司從國外引進了新設備。
column6: Gōngsī cóng guówài yǐnjìn le xīn shèbèi.
column7: The company brought in new equipment from abroad.

column3: To attract, draw: 吸引游客 "attract tourists", 吸引注意 "draw attention", 被吸引 "be drawn", 有吸引力 "attractive". 吸 "suck in" plus 引 "draw". The thing that attracts is the subject, and the people or things drawn are the object. Used for people, places and ideas.
column4: 这座城市吸引了很多游客。
column5: 這座城市吸引了很多遊客。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì xīyǐn le hěn duō yóukè.
column7: This city attracts many tourists.

column3: To absorb, take in: 吸收水分 "absorb water", 吸收知识 "take in knowledge", 吸收新成员 "admit new members". 吸 "suck" plus 收 "receive". It works for physical things (a sponge, plants) and for abstract ones (ideas, experience), and for groups taking in members.
column6: Hǎimián kěyǐ xīshōu hěn duō shuǐ.
column7: A sponge can absorb a lot of water.

column3: To bring into play, give full play to: 发挥作用 "play a role", 发挥才能 "make use of one's talents", 发挥得很好 "perform well". 发 "send out" plus 挥 "wave". Used for abilities, roles and strengths, and for performance in exams and matches: 今天发挥不好.
column4: 他在比赛中发挥得很好。
column5: 他在比賽中發揮得很好。
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng fāhuī de hěn hǎo.
column7: He performed very well in the match.

column3: To use, apply knowledge, skills or methods: 运用知识 "apply knowledge", 运用技巧, 灵活运用 "use flexibly". 运 "move" plus 用 "use". It stresses putting something learned to practical use, more than 用 or 使用.
column4: 你要学会运用学到的知识。
column5: 你要學會運用學到的知識。
column6: Nǐ yào xuéhuì yùnyòng xuédào de zhīshi.
column7: You should learn to apply the knowledge you've gained.

column3: Practical, useful: 实用的礼物 "a practical gift", 很实用 "very practical", 实用性. 实 "real" plus 用 "use". It describes things with a real daily use, in contrast to something pretty. A neutral and positive word, used of objects, skills, books.
column4: 这本书很实用，我每天都用。
column5: 這本書很實用，我每天都用。
column6: Zhè běn shū hěn shíyòng, wǒ měitiān dōu yòng.
column7: This book is very practical, and I use it every day.

column3: Use, purpose of a thing: 有很多用途 "has many uses", 主要用途 "main use", 用途广泛 "widely used". 用 "use" plus 途 "way". It answers the question "what is it used for?". The 途 radical 辶 reflects the idea of a road or path.
column6: Zhè zhǒng gōngjù yǒu hěn duō yòngtú.
column7: This tool has many uses.

column3: To make, come up with a decision, response or contribution: 作出决定 "make a decision", 作出贡献 "make a contribution", 作出回应, 作出努力. 作 "do" plus the result 出 "out". The object is something abstract, such as a decision, reply or promise. Formal; 做出 is the same, and 作出 is the written form.
column4: 公司作出了一个重要的决定。
column5: 公司作出了一個重要的決定。
column6: Gōngsī zuòchū le yī ge zhòngyào de juédìng.
column7: The company made an important decision.

column3: To draw, pull, lead; to cite: 引起 "cause", 引导 "guide", 吸引 "attract", 引用 "quote", 引火 "light a fire". As a verb on its own it means "to attract" or "to quote": 引出话题 "lead into a topic". The picture is a bow 弓 and a line: a bow being drawn.
column6: Zhè jù huà yǐn zì yī běn gǔ shū.
column7: This sentence is quoted from an old book.

column3: To include, comprise: 包括……在内 "including ...", 价格包括早餐 "the price includes breakfast", 包括我 "including me". 包 "wrap" plus 括 "enclose". It lists items inside a larger group, with examples. Don't use it for a person as a subject; the subject is a whole group.
column6: Jiàgé bāokuò zǎocān hé wǎncān.
column7: The price includes breakfast and dinner.

column3: To contain, include: 包含意思 "contain a meaning", 包含着 "contain", 包含很多信息. 包 "wrap" plus 含 "hold". The container holds something as a part or an element, often something abstract or hidden. Compare 包括, which lists parts.
column4: 这句话包含着很深的意思。
column5: 這句話包含著很深的意思。
column6: Zhè jù huà bāohán zhe hěn shēn de yìsi.
column7: This sentence contains a deep meaning.

column3: To hold in the mouth; to contain: 含着糖 "with a candy in the mouth", 含水 "contain water", 含笑 "with a smile", 含糊 "vague". 含 is 今 over 口 (mouth): something in the mouth. The sound part 今 (jīn) has moved a long way from hán. The verb is used on its own for the mouth, and in compounds for "contain".
column6: Háizi zuǐ lǐ hán zhe yī kuài táng.
column7: The child has a candy in his mouth.

column3: To contain: 含有糖分 "contain sugar", 含有水分, 含有毒素. 含 "hold" plus 有 "have". It is about substances in food, water and goods, and ingredients on a label. Followed by a thing or a quantity word.
column6: Zhè zhǒng yǐnliào hányǒu hěn duō táng.
column7: This drink contains a lot of sugar.

column3: To conform to, meet a standard, requirement or situation: 符合要求 "meet the requirements", 符合条件 "fulfill the conditions", 符合实际 "fit reality". 符 "tally" plus 合 "match". The two things match exactly, as a seal matches its imprint. The object is almost always an abstract standard.
column4: 他的条件完全符合要求。
column5: 他的條件完全符合要求。
column6: Tā de tiáojiàn wánquán fúhé yāoqiú.
column7: His qualifications fully meet the requirements.

column3: To have, possess a quality, ability or condition: 具备条件 "meet the conditions", 具备能力 "have the ability", 不具备. 具 "provide" plus 备 "prepare". Said of conditions, abilities or equipment, not physical objects. It is formal.
column4: 做这份工作要具备一定的能力。
column5: 做這份工作要具備一定的能力。
column6: Zuò zhè fèn gōngzuò yào jùbèi yīdìng de nénglì.
column7: To do this job, you need to have a certain ability.

column3: Consistent, in agreement: 意见一致 "agree in opinion", 一致同意 "unanimously agree", 前后一致 "consistent". 一 "one" plus 致 "reach". An adjective, it follows the subject, and as an adverb it means "unanimously". The opposite is 不一致.
column6: Dàjiā de yìjiàn wánquán yīzhì.
column7: Everyone's opinions are completely in agreement.

column3: To compare, contrast; contrast: 形成对比 "form a contrast", 对比一下 "compare", 鲜明的对比 "a sharp contrast". 对 "face" plus 比 "compare". The two things are put side by side to show differences. Also a ratio in sports, "score": 比分.
column4: 把这两张照片对比一下。
column5: 把這兩張照片對比一下。
column6: Bǎ zhè liǎng zhāng zhàopiàn duìbǐ yīxià.
column7: Compare these two photos.

column3: Opposite, contrary: 相反的方向 "the opposite direction", 正好相反 "just the opposite", 恰恰相反. As an adjective it follows 与……相反. At the start of a sentence, "on the contrary": 相反，他很高兴. 相 "mutually" plus 反 "reverse".
column4: 他和我的想法正好相反。
column5: 他和我的想法正好相反。
column6: Tā hé wǒ de xiǎngfǎ zhènghǎo xiāngfǎn.
column7: His idea is the exact opposite of mine.

column3: Opposite, reverse; to oppose: 反对 "oppose", 反面 "reverse side", 反应 "react", 反问 "ask in return", 反穿 "wear inside out". It also forms "anti-": 反战. On its own it is often a result: 穿反了 "put on the wrong way round". The hand 又 under a cliff 厂: in the picture, a hand held up against a cliff.
column6: Nǐ de yīfu chuān fǎn le.
column7: You've put your clothes on inside out.

column3: To reflect; to report: 反映现实 "reflect reality", 反映问题 "raise a problem", 向领导反映 "report to the leaders". 反 "reverse" plus 映 "shine". An image is thrown back like a mirror. It is also a way of telling superiors about a complaint.
column4: 这部电影反映了现实生活。
column5: 這部電影反映了現實生活。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng fǎnyìng le xiànshí shēnghuó.
column7: This film reflects real life.

column3: To deal with, handle; to make do: 对付困难 "deal with a difficulty", 不好对付 "hard to handle", 对付一下 "just make do (with)". 对 "face" plus 付 "hand over". The object is a person, problem or situation, and the tone is a bit informal. In 对付一顿 it means "get by on".
column6: Zhège háizi hěn bù hǎo duìfu.
column7: This child is hard to handle.

column3: Meaning, implication of a word, phrase or gesture: 词的含义 "the meaning of a word", 深刻的含义, 有两种含义. 含 "hold" plus 义 "meaning": a meaning that is held inside. It suggests something implicit, more than 意思 does. The measure is 种 or 层.
column4: 这个词有两种不同的含义。
column5: 這個詞有兩種不同的含義。
column6: Zhège cí yǒu liǎng zhǒng bù tóng de hányì.
column7: This word has two different meanings.

column3: Content, amount contained: 含糖量 "sugar content", 维生素含量 "vitamin content", 含量高 "high in". 含 "contain" plus 量 "amount". It is a measure of how much of a substance is in something, in food labels and in science.
column4: 这种水果的维生素含量很高。
column5: 這種水果的維生素含量很高。
column6: Zhè zhǒng shuǐguǒ de wéishēngsù hánliàng hěn gāo.
column7: This fruit is high in vitamin content.

column3: To obtain, gain, win: 获得成功 "achieve success", 获得奖学金 "get a scholarship", 获得帮助 "receive help". 获 "obtain" plus 得 "get". The object is good, valuable and often abstract: a prize, an experience, a right. It is formal compared with 得到.
column4: 她在比赛中获得了第一名。
column5: 她在比賽中獲得了第一名。
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng huòdé le dì-yī míng.
column7: She won first place in the competition.

column3: To obtain, acquire information, resources or data: 获取信息 "get information", 获取知识, 获取资源. 获 "obtain" plus 取 "take". You actively seek it out, typically from a source. Often used with technology: 获取密码.
column4: 我们可以在网上获取很多信息。
column5: 我們可以在網上獲取很多資訊。
column6: Wǒmen kěyǐ zài wǎng shang huòqǔ hěn duō xìnxī.
column7: We can get a lot of information online.

column3: To take back, withdraw: 收回借出的钱 "get back money lent", 收回成命 "withdraw an order", 收回话 "take back one's words". 收 "receive" plus the result 回 "back". Used for money, things lent and statements. The object is what you had given.
column4: 他想收回借给朋友的钱。
column5: 他想收回借給朋友的錢。
column6: Tā xiǎng shōuhuí jiè gěi péngyou de qián.
column7: He wants to get back the money he lent to his friend.

column3: Harvest; gain, what one takes away: 秋天是收获的季节 "autumn is the harvest season", 这次旅行收获很大 "I gained a lot from this trip". The verb means to harvest crops or to reap results. 收 "gather" plus 获 "obtain". The figurative sense is for lessons, experience or friendships, and the verb is often 有: 有很多收获.
column6: Zhè cì lǚxíng wǒ shōuhuò hěn dà.
column7: I gained a lot from this trip.

column3: To provide, supply, offer: 提供帮助 "offer help", 提供服务 "provide a service", 提供信息. 提 "put forward" plus 供 "supply". Here 供 is read gōng. The subject is a person, company or place, and the object is a service, material or information. The thing is given to others at your initiative.
column4: 酒店为客人提供免费早餐。
column5: 酒店為客人提供免費早餐。
column6: Jiǔdiàn wèi kèrén tígōng miǎnfèi zǎocān.
column7: The hotel provides free breakfast for its guests.

column3: To supply, provide goods or services in quantity: 供应食品 "supply food", 供应充足 "plentiful supply", 供应商 "supplier". 供 "supply" plus 应 "respond". The 应 is yìng here, "answer a need". It describes the continued supply of things like water, electricity and meals.
column4: 这里二十四小时供应热水。
column5: 這裡二十四小時供應熱水。
column6: Zhèlǐ èrshísì xiǎoshí gōngyìng rèshuǐ.
column7: Hot water is supplied here around the clock.

column3: To exchange, swap: 交换礼物 "exchange gifts", 交换意见 "exchange views", 交换学生 "exchange student". 交 "hand over" plus 换 "change". Both sides give and receive, so it is two-way. For a one-way change, use 换.
column4: 我们互相交换了电话号码。
column5: 我們互相交換了電話號碼。
column6: Wǒmen hùxiāng jiāohuàn le diànhuà hàomǎ.
column7: We exchanged phone numbers with each other.

column3: To send by post, mail: 寄信 "send a letter", 寄包裹 "mail a parcel", 寄给他 "send to him". Also "to entrust": 寄希望于 "pin hopes on". The roof radical 宀 goes with the older sense of staying away from home, in someone's care.
column6: Wǒ gěi péngyou jì le yī fēng xìn.
column7: I sent my friend a letter.

column3: To put in; to devote oneself; absorbed: 投入时间 "put in time", 投入资金 "invest money", 工作很投入 "very absorbed in work", 投入使用 "put into use". 投 "throw" plus 入 "enter". It is used both for an investment of money or effort and for being fully engaged in an activity.
column6: Tā zuòshì zǒngshì fēicháng tóurù.
column7: He is always fully absorbed in what he does.

column3: To return; to belong to: 回归 "return", 归还 "give back", 归国 "return to one's country", 这些书归你 "these books are yours". The second sense, "to be the responsibility of / belong to," is common in the spoken language.
column6: Zhèxiē shū yǐhòu dōu guī nǐ le.
column7: From now on these books are all yours.

column3: To pursue, seek: 追求梦想 "pursue a dream", 追求幸福 "pursue happiness", 追求完美 "strive for perfection". Also "to court someone": 追求她. 追 "chase" plus 求 "seek". The object is a goal or ideal, a long-term aim. It is a formal and positive word.
column4: 他一直在追求自己的梦想。
column5: 他一直在追求自己的夢想。
column6: Tā yīzhí zài zhuīqiú zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng.
column7: He has always been pursuing his own dream.

column3: To look for, seek: 寻找工作 "look for a job", 寻找答案 "search for an answer", 寻找机会. 寻 and 找 both mean "look for". It is more formal and literary than 找 and suggests a longer search, especially for something abstract or lost. For small things like keys, say 找.
column4: 我们正在寻找新的办法。
column5: 我們正在尋找新的辦法。
column6: Wǒmen zhèngzài xúnzhǎo xīn de bànfǎ.
column7: We are looking for a new way.

column3: To throw, cast, put in: 投票 "vote", 投篮 "shoot a basket", 投信 "post a letter", 投资 "invest", 投入 "devote". It covers throwing something to a target and putting it in a slot. 投他一票 "vote for him". The hand 扌 on the left; 殳 on the right is the sound part.
column6: Wǒ tóu le tā yī piào.
column7: I cast a vote for him.

column3: Outstanding, excellent: 优秀学生 "outstanding student", 成绩优秀 "excellent grades", 优秀作品. 优 "superior" plus 秀 "excellent". It praises people and their work, in school and work. Stronger than 好 and used in awards, evaluations and reports.
column4: 她是班里最优秀的学生。
column5: 她是班裡最優秀的學生。
column6: Tā shì bān lǐ zuì yōuxiù de xuésheng.
column7: She is the best student in the class.

column3: Fine, of good quality: 优良传统 "fine tradition", 品质优良 "of good quality", 优良品种 "a superior variety". 优 "superior" plus 良 "good". It praises qualities such as a tradition, a variety or a record, and is mostly written.
column6: Zhōngguó yǒu hěn duō yōuliáng chuántǒng.
column7: China has many fine traditions.

column3: Good, favorable: 良好的习惯 "good habits", 关系良好 "good relations", 状态良好 "in good condition". 良 "good" plus 好 "good". An adjective for qualities, conditions and habits, used in writing and in school marks: 良好 is the grade below 优秀. It is formal.
column4: 他从小养成了良好的习惯。
column5: 他從小養成了良好的習慣。
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo yǎngchéng le liánghǎo de xíguàn.
column7: He developed good habits from childhood.

column3: Graceful, beautiful, for scenery, music, writing and movement: 风景优美 "beautiful scenery", 优美的音乐, 动作优美. 优 "excellent" plus 美 "beautiful". It describes a gentle, refined beauty that you see or hear, not a striking one. It is not used for people's looks, which is 漂亮.
column4: 这里风景优美，空气新鲜。
column5: 這裡風景優美，空氣新鮮。
column6: Zhèlǐ fēngjǐng yōuměi, kōngqì xīnxiān.
column7: The scenery here is beautiful and the air is fresh.

column3: Outstanding, remarkable: 表现出色 "perform outstandingly", 出色地完成 "accomplish brilliantly", 非常出色. 出 "go beyond" plus 色 "color/appearance": it stands out. Said of work, performance and people. Unlike 优秀, it highlights standing out among others.
column4: 他出色地完成了这个任务。
column5: 他出色地完成了這個任務。
column6: Tā chūsè de wánchéng le zhège rènwu.
column7: He carried out this task outstandingly.

column3: Satisfactory, perfect, complete: 圆满成功 "a complete success", 圆满完成 "complete satisfactorily", 圆满结束. 圆 "round" plus 满 "full". A round shape and a full one: nothing missing. It describes how an event or task ends, not an object. Often seen with 取得: 取得圆满成功.
column6: Huìyì yuánmǎn jiéshù le.
column7: The meeting ended with complete success.

column3: Typical; a typical example: 典型例子 "a typical example", 典型的北方人 "a typical northerner", 很典型. 典 "model" plus 型 "type". It describes something that represents its kind well, and as a noun it is the model case. It can be used in a good or bad sense: 典型的懒人.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge diǎnxíng de lìzi.
column7: This is a typical example.

column3: Special, particular, unusual: 特殊情况 "a special case", 特殊的方法, 特殊待遇 "special treatment". 特 "special" plus 殊 "different". It stresses that something is unlike the usual, often for a reason, not that it is wonderful. Common for rules and situations.
column4: 这种情况比较特殊，需要特别处理。
column5: 這種情況比較特殊，需要特別處理。
column6: Zhè zhǒng qíngkuàng bǐjiào tèshū, xūyào tèbié chǔlǐ.
column7: This situation is rather special and needs special handling.

column3: Unique, distinctive: 独特的风格 "a distinctive style", 独特的魅力 "unique charm", 很独特. 独 "alone" plus 特 "special". It praises something for being unlike all others, with its own character. Used for styles, tastes, ideas and places.
column4: 这家店的菜有独特的味道。
column5: 這家店的菜有獨特的味道。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de cài yǒu dútè de wèidào.
column7: The food at this shop has a unique taste.

column3: Bright, distinct, vivid: 色彩鲜明 "bright colors", 立场鲜明 "a clear stance", 鲜明的对比 "a sharp contrast", 特点鲜明. 鲜 "fresh" plus 明 "clear". It describes colors, differences and attitudes that are clear to see, with no doubt about them.
column4: 这幅画的色彩非常鲜明。
column5: 這幅畫的色彩非常鮮明。
column6: Zhè fú huà de sècǎi fēicháng xiānmíng.
column7: The colors in this painting are very vivid.

column3: Notable, marked, significant: 显著提高 "improve markedly", 效果显著 "the effect is clear", 显著的变化. 显 "show" plus 著 "outstanding". It says a change or effect is easy to notice, and it is used with 提高, 进步, 变化. In statistics, it means "statistically significant".
column4: 他的汉语水平有了显著的提高。
column5: 他的漢語水平有了顯著的提高。
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ shuǐpíng yǒu le xiǎnzhù de tígāo.
column7: His Chinese level has improved markedly.

column3: To like, be fond of: 好学 "love learning", 好动 "active", 好客 "hospitable", 好奇 "curious", 爱好 "hobby". In this sense it is read hào and it comes before a verb, with the sense of habit or fondness. 好 is read hǎo for "good".
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù hào dúshū.
column7: He has liked reading since he was little.

column3: Pure, unmixed: 纯水 "pure water", 纯棉 "pure cotton", 纯金 "pure gold", 纯正 "authentic", 纯真 "innocent". It states that nothing else is mixed in. The thread 纟 on the left reflects its origin in silk and fabrics. The sound part is 屯 (tún), which no longer sounds quite like chún.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì chúnmián de.
column7: This piece of clothing is pure cotton.

column3: Transparent: 透明的玻璃 "transparent glass", 透明塑料袋 "clear plastic bag", and figuratively "open, transparent": 价格透明 "transparent pricing". 透 "pass through" plus 明 "clear". Light passes through it. For people, 公开 is used.
column6: Zhège bēizi shì tòumíng de.
column7: This cup is transparent.

column3: Monotonous, dull: 单调的生活 "a monotonous life", 声音单调, 颜色单调, 太单调了. 单 "single" plus 调 "tone". The 调 is read diào here. Only one tone or one pattern, with nothing varied. It is a negative word, used for jobs, music, colors and routines.
column4: 每天做同样的事，生活太单调了。
column5: 每天做同樣的事，生活太單調了。
column6: Měitiān zuò tóngyàng de shì, shēnghuó tài dāndiào le.
column7: Doing the same thing every day, life is too monotonous.

column3: Strange, odd and "to blame": 奇怪 "strange", 怪事 "a strange thing", 别怪我 "don't blame me", 怪不得 "no wonder". In speech 怪 can also mean "rather, quite": 怪可爱的 "rather cute". The heart radical 忄 adds a sense of an odd feeling. It is placed before adjectives and as a verb.
column6: Zhè bù néng guài tā, shì wǒ de cuò.
column7: You can't blame him, it was my fault.

column3: Strict, tight, severe: 严格 "strict", 严重 "serious", 严肃 "solemn", 门关严 "close the door tight", 严父 "stern father". As a complement it means "tightly, with no gaps": 关严, 盖严. It is a bound word in most compounds.
column4: 门没有关严，风吹进来了。
column5: 門沒有關嚴，風吹進來了。
column6: Mén méiyǒu guān yán, fēng chuī jìnlái le.
column7: The door wasn't closed tight and the wind blew in.

column3: Strict, rigorous: 严格要求 "demand strictly", 管理严格 "strictly managed", 严格执行 "enforce strictly". 严 "strict" plus 格 "standard". It describes people and rules that allow no leniency. As an adverb, it comes before a verb: 严格遵守. The opposite is 宽松.
column4: 老师对我们的要求很严格。
column5: 老師對我們的要求很嚴格。
column6: Lǎoshī duì wǒmen de yāoqiú hěn yángé.
column7: The teacher is very strict with us.

column3: Serious, grave, severe: 严重的问题 "a serious problem", 病得很严重 "seriously ill", 严重影响 "seriously affect". 严 "severe" plus 重 "heavy". Said of bad things such as illness, damage and mistakes. It is not used for a person's manner (that is 严肃).
column6: Tā de bìngqíng hěn yánzhòng.
column7: His illness is very serious.

column3: Secret: 保守秘密 "keep a secret", 小秘密, 一个秘密, 秘密地 "secretly". 秘 "hidden" plus 密 "dense, close". As a noun it is the secret itself, and as an adjective it means secret. Telling a secret is 告诉你一个秘密. In 秘书 "secretary" the same character is read mì too.
column4: 我告诉你一个秘密，你别说出去。
column5: 我告訴你一個秘密，你別說出去。
column6: Wǒ gàosu nǐ yī ge mìmì, nǐ bié shuō chūqù.
column7: I'll tell you a secret, don't tell anyone.

column3: Mysterious: 神秘的人 "a mysterious person", 神秘的礼物, 很神秘, 神秘感. 神 "spirit" plus 秘 "hidden". Something seems unexplained or hidden, with a sense of wonder or unease. Differs from 秘密, which means the secret itself.
column4: 山里有一个神秘的小村子。
column5: 山裡有一個神秘的小村子。
column6: Shān lǐ yǒu yī ge shénmì de xiǎo cūnzi.
column7: There is a mysterious little village in the mountains.

column3: To keep secret: 请保密 "please keep it confidential", 保密协议 "confidentiality agreement", 对外保密. 保 "protect" plus 密 "secret". A verb-object word, so it can be split: 保了密. Said of information that must not be disclosed, in work or in personal matters.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì qǐng nǐ yīdìng bǎomì.
column7: Please keep this matter strictly secret.

column3: Close, intimate for relationships and links: 关系密切 "closely related", 密切合作 "cooperate closely", 密切注意 "watch closely". 密 "close" plus 切 "close/keen". The 切 is read qiè here, not qiē. It describes relations, contact and attention, not physical closeness; for people sitting close, 靠近 is used.
column4: 这两个国家的关系非常密切。
column5: 這兩個國家的關係非常密切。
column6: Zhè liǎng ge guójiā de guānxi fēicháng mìqiè.
column7: The relations between these two countries are very close.

column3: Independent; to stand on one's own: 独立生活 "live independently", 独立思考 "think for oneself", 国家独立 "national independence". 独 "alone" plus 立 "stand". A person can be independent from parents, and a country from another. As a verb it takes no object. Often a positive trait: 他很独立.
column4: 他十八岁就开始独立生活了。
column5: 他十八歲就開始獨立生活了。
column6: Tā shíbā suì jiù kāishǐ dúlì shēnghuó le.
column7: He started to live independently at eighteen.

column3: Dense, close; secret: 密集 "densely packed", 密切 "close", 秘密 "secret", 密码 "password", 保密 "keep secret". On its own it describes things packed closely: 头发很密 "thick hair", 树林很密. It has 山 "mountain" inside it: something hidden in the mountains, which fits both "dense" and "secret".
column4: 这片树林很密，很难走进去。
column5: 這片樹林很密，很難走進去。
column6: Zhè piàn shùlín hěn mì, hěn nán zǒu jìnqù.
column7: This wood is dense and hard to walk into.

column3: Close, tight, closely knit: 紧密合作 "work closely together", 联系紧密 "closely linked", 紧密结合. 紧 "tight" plus 密 "dense". It stresses a link with no gaps, between people, organizations or parts. Often used as an adverb or modifier in writing.
column4: 两个公司的合作越来越紧密。
column5: 兩個公司的合作越來越緊密。
column6: Liǎng ge gōngsī de hézuò yuè lái yuè jǐnmì.
column7: The cooperation between the two companies is getting closer and closer.

column3: To seal off, close; closed: 封闭道路 "close a road", 封闭管理 "closed-off management", 思想封闭 "narrow-minded". 封 "seal" plus 闭 "shut". Officials close roads, buildings and areas for safety or control. Used of a person, "closed in", meaning cut off from new ideas.
column4: 因为下雪，高速公路被封闭了。
column5: 因為下雪，高速公路被封閉了。
column6: Yīnwèi xià xuě, gāosùgōnglù bèi fēngbì le.
column7: The expressway was closed because of snow.

column3: Conservative (cautious, not open to change) and "to keep" a secret: 保守秘密 "keep a secret", 思想保守 "conservative in thinking", 保守的人. 保 "protect" plus 守 "guard". As an adjective, it criticizes mildly; in politics it can be neutral. The verb form is mostly with 秘密.
column4: 我爷爷的想法比较保守。
column5: 我爺爺的想法比較保守。
column6: Wǒ yéye de xiǎngfǎ bǐjiào bǎoshǒu.
column7: My grandfather's ideas are rather conservative.

column3: To be particular about; carefully chosen: 讲究卫生 "pay attention to hygiene", 吃得很讲究 "eat with great care", 穿着讲究 "dress with taste". As a noun, "something to take care over": 这里面有讲究 "there is a point to this". 讲 "talk" plus 究 "investigate". A neutral tone on 究. Positive or slightly picky.
column4: 她吃饭很讲究，只吃新鲜的菜。
column5: 她吃飯很講究，只吃新鮮的菜。
column6: Tā chīfàn hěn jiǎngjiu, zhǐ chī xīnxiān de cài.
column7: She is particular about her food and eats only fresh dishes.
